evidence.title: SSE stream abruptly closes and final tokens dropped for long assistant responses
evidence.text:
description:
Issue summary:
Customers report that SSE (text/event-stream) chat sessions serving long-form assistant responses are terminating before the final tokens are emitted. The client sees the stream close suddenly and the response is missing last paragraphs (usually >800 tokens). No explicit 5xx error returned to the client; connection terminates and client-side library reports EOF. Impact: multiple production customers on Dedicated capacity experienced truncated replies in the afternoon of 2026-03-10. This affects UX for long assistant outputs (summaries, long-form generation) and caused one customer to revert to polling for short-term mitigation.

Impact:
- BrightByte Health observed ~12% of long streaming responses truncated between 15:10–16:40 PDT on 2026-03-10.
- Increased support volume and PagerDuty alerts from Customer Success and SRE.

Environment/Context:
- Dedicated pool: d-pool-us-west-2-3
- API path: /v1/chat/stream (SSE) behind service-gateway (Envoy + NGINX ingress in front of gateway for legacy customers)
- Observed primarily with long context and responses that trigger continuous token emission for >14s. Short replies unaffected.

Expected behavior:
- SSE stream should remain open until server emits the final event and properly flushes trailing data.

Observed behavior:
- Stream abruptly closes mid-response; client receives truncated content and no clear server-side 5xx. Upstream logs show upstream connection closed with reset by peer in some cases.

Additional notes:
- Customers use standard Accept: text/event-stream; some are behind corporate proxies which show similar failures but at a lower rate.


steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a chat session using /v1/chat/stream with an instruction that elicits a long response (>800 tokens).
2) Use curl or a JS EventSource client to consume the stream.
3) Observe that after a burst of token events, the connection may close before the final 'done' event is sent; reproduced more reliably under moderate concurrent load (30-50 rps) against the dedicated pool.
4) Repeat with same prompt against a shorter-response prompt to confirm no truncation.


logs:
- service-gateway (proxy) logs: several entries 'upstream prematurely closed connection' and 'connection termination: downstream reset' correlated with timestamps 2026-03-10 15:17:33–15:40:12 PDT.
- Serving-runtime logs (worker-7): 'flush interval exceeded, coalesced chunks sent' followed by 'write failed: connection reset by peer' with no additional error.
- Envoy stats: increases in 504-overriden timeouts and connection failures on listener 8443.
- No application-level 5xx returned to clients in many truncated cases; tcp-level FIN/RST is observed.


investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered:
- Idle/proxy timeout in NGINX/Envoy/Corporate proxy cutting long-lived streaming connections when chunk sizes are small.
- Serving runtime flush behavior emits many small chunks; some intermediaries buffer and then decide to close based on perceived inactivity.
- Network path MTU or TLS renegotiation edge-case causing TCP reset under bursty token emission.

What we tested:
- Increased keepalive and proxy idle timeouts on a staging gateway and re-ran the prompt: truncation rate dropped significantly.
- Instrumented worker to coalesce token writes to larger chunks (flush every 128 tokens or 250ms whichever first) in a canary build: replication improved.
- Captured pcap on a test environment: confirmed RSTs originate from the gateway process when upstream read/write queue spikes.

Interim conclusion:
- Root cause is a combination of small-chunk flushing from the serving runtime and conservative timeouts/buffering behavior in the gateway (Envoy/NGINX combo) which, under moderate concurrency, leads to upstream connection resets and silent stream termination.


comments:
Aisha Ramey (customer): We're seeing truncated clinical summaries in production when we ask the model for long outputs. Happens ~1 in 8 requests. Impacting our demo tomorrow.
Riley Chen (support): Received logs and reproduction steps. Escalating to SRE; capturing traces. Please provide example request IDs if you can.
SRE (Luca Moretti): Reproduced in canary by driving 40 rps against d-pool-us-west-2-3. Saw gateway produce connection resets when write queue grew. Increasing proxy idle timeout and coalescing flushes reduces failures.
Customer Success (Maya Patel): Provided three example request IDs and confirmed business impact. Asked for ETA on fix or recommended mitigation.
Riley Chen: Rolled out gateway config change (increase idle_timeout to 90s and disable proxy_buffering for SSE routes) to affected Dedicated pools as an immediate mitigation. Also toggled canary runtime build to coalesce writes in staging for verification.

resolution:
Immediate mitigation: increased proxy idle_timeout to 90s for SSE endpoints and disabled response buffering on ingress NGINX for dedicated pools. Recommendation issued to customers experiencing truncation: re-open session or fallback to polling if intermittent.

Longer-term fix implemented: serving-runtime change to coalesce token writes (flush policy: max 128 tokens or 250ms) merged to main (github.com/redwood-inference/service-runtime/pull/822) and deployed to Dedicated pools during maintenance window on 2026-03-12. Gateway rollback protections and improved observability (per-token lag metrics) added.

Post-deploy validation: truncation rate for BrightByte Health fell from 12% to <0.5% in the 24h after the deploy. No related rollouts required for Hosted customers.

Follow-ups: Add a streaming SLO and synthetic that exercises long SSE responses across all dedicated pools; document HTTP proxy recommendations for customers that front Redwood with corporate proxies.

evidence.title: Partial final output missing after SSE reconnect during TLS renegotiation behind edge proxy
evidence.text:
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that when a streaming SSE connection briefly drops during a TLS renegotiation event at the edge, the client receives a truncated final output: the last sentence or final punctuation is missing and no explicit end marker arrives. The server logs show the completion event emitted, but the client-side stream terminates early after reconnect.

Impact:
- Affects Inkling Health's production inference pipelines in eu-west.
- Partial outputs break downstream post-processing and fail schema validation for their clinical note ingestion (automated).
- Observed on ~3% of long-running streaming sessions during peak load windows.

Environment:
- prod (eu-west) behind vendor edge proxy (CloudEdge) + vendor CDN.
- Clients use SSE long-polling from browser and also a Node.js backend that implements reconnect/resume.
- Model: rw-instruct-large-v1, typical max_tokens ~1024, average response length ~600 tokens.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a long streaming generation from eu-west with prefix that yields a long final sentence.
2) Simulate TLS renegotiation at the edge by triggering a short RST/reconnect (they used their synthetic traffic tool to flip the client IP and trigger a rehandshake).
3) Observe returned stream on client: most of the time it resumes fine, but in a subset the final sentence is cut off and no terminal event arrives.

Expected behavior:
- Client should receive full streamed tokens including terminal metadata (choice completion). Reconnect/resume should either stitch output seamlessly or include an explicit end marker.

Actual behavior:
- Server emits completion and logs show terminal event for the request id, but the client sees an abrupt stop after an earlier chunk. No explicit "[DONE]" or terminal JSON arrives. Reconnect handshake shows success, but resumed stream never emits the missing trailing tokens.

Workaround (customer):
- Increase client-side post-reconnect polling window and re-request tail tokens using non-streaming completion API; this recovers text but adds latency and cost.

Attachments:
- customer provided curl and Node.js reproducer, sample client traces, and a HAR file (attached separately in support portal).

steps_to_reproduce:
Open SSE stream to /v1/stream with a long prompt that generates a long final sentence
From a test machine behind the same edge, flip IP or trigger short RST to force TLS rehandshake at the edge
Allow reconnect to occur and observe client-side stream events and final terminal event presence
Repeat under load to increase probability of occurrence

logs:
2026-03-12T08:23:45Z serving-runtime: request=req_6f3a terminal_emitted=true seq=0x1ee logsize=1024
2026-03-12T08:23:45Z api-gateway: proxy_write returned 0 bytes to edge worker (code=EPIPE) connection_id=conn_9b
2026-03-12T08:23:46Z edge-proxy: TLS renegotiate start connection_id=conn_9b client_ip=203.0.113.45
2026-03-12T08:23:46Z edge-proxy: coalesced-keepalive zero-length write observed, buffering=true
2026-03-12T08:23:46Z serving-runtime: request=req_6f3a connection_lost_event=true, terminal_delivery_confirmed=false

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: edge proxy zero-length write or buffering during TLS renegotiation causes downstream client to interpret stream as complete. Reproduced in lab by enabling 'edge-worker buffering' and forcing a TLS rehandshake; observed identical symptom. Further narrowed to case where proxy coalesces an SSI keepalive packet with the final JSON boundary, then performs connection migration and the client-side SSE parser treats the next boundary as a new stream rather than continuation.

What we checked:
- Server emits final JSON and exits stream (confirmed).
- Gateway recorded a 0-byte write to the edge worker immediately prior to client disconnect.
- Client reconnects and requests resume token, but resume offset points to earlier chunk (off-by-one) because the proxy suppressed the terminal delimiter during buffering.

Immediate mitigation tried:
- Applied an API-gateway config to insert an explicit "event: end" / "data: [DONE]" line before flushing final chunk for eu-west. Reduced occurrence rate from ~3% to ~0.1% in canary traffic.

Next steps:
- Collaborate with edge-proxy vendor to disable coalescing of zero-length keepalives for SSE endpoints, or to preserve final JSON boundaries across renegotiation.
- Add extra server-side terminal marker for SSE (backport to stable) to make client reconcilers robust to proxy buffering.
- Add more robust resume offset verification on server to ensure resume doesn't skip final tokens.

resolution:
Mitigation applied: gateway now injects an explicit SSE end marker before connection handoff in eu-west canary. Customer workaround documented. Root cause vendor coordination required for permanent fix.

resolution_notes:
Applied canary change 2026-03-13 21:12 UTC to eu-west API-gateway fleet: insert explicit terminal SSE event prior to drain. Monitoring shows reduced error rate. Opening a vendor support ticket with CloudEdge (ticket CE-5542) to request fix for zero-length coalescing during TLS renegotiate. Engineering to prepare backport for streaming runtime to include optional double-terminal marker.

comments:
2026-03-12 10:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reports truncated final sentence on SSE resumes when client TLS renegotiates at the edge. Attaching reproducer and HAR.
2026-03-12 11:05 - Daniel Park (SRE): Reproduced in staging with edge-worker buffering enabled. See logs. Hypothesis: proxy coalescing zero-length keepalive into stream boundary.
2026-03-13 09:20 - Inkling Health (Customer): We can confirm workaround of re-requesting tail tokens; production impact is reduced but not acceptable for latency-sensitive processing.
2026-03-13 22:00 - Daniel Park (SRE): Deployed canary gateway change to inject explicit SSE terminal event prior to handoff to edge. Monitoring in progress.
2026-03-14 07:30 - Priya Mehta (Platform Eng): Suggest adding server-side resume offset validation and an idempotent terminal marker — preparing a small patch for review (PR referenced).

evidence.title: Intermittent websocket half-close after corporate TLS rekey -> trailing 'done' envelope never arrives
evidence.text:
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent websocket sessions that appear to close from the server side after a TLS rekey performed by their corporate TLS-inspecting proxy. The stream is truncated: the final JSON envelope with status/done metadata is never received, leaving the client waiting indefinitely. Impact: Multiple production users at Acme AI Labs experience truncated generations and must reissue requests; affects business-critical inference pipelines. Observed first at ~2026-03-09 22:15 PST and recurred several times. Environment: prod cluster behind ALB -> CloudFront -> corporate TLS-inspection -> customer client. No code changes on Redwood side around times of first occurrence.

steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer establishes long-running websocket streaming request against /v1/streams with model redwood-1-large. 2) While the model is streaming a ~4000-token completion, customer network triggers TLS session renegotiation / rekey (corporate proxy performs active MITM). 3) Connection experiences a short TCP-level close followed by client reconnect; client tries to resume but never receives final 'done' envelope or terminal metadata. 4) Repeating with curl/wscat behind same proxy triggers the same truncated stream ~30% of runs. Reproducer cURL/websocket notes included in logs.

logs:
[2026-03-09T22:15:12.457Z] conn=abcd1234 ws-session open token=redacted
[2026-03-09T22:17:45.791Z] upstream-proxy: TLS_REKEY observed, client-ip=10.8.1.24
[2026-03-09T22:17:45.892Z] conn=abcd1234 ws half-close detected (FIN from client-path)
[2026-03-09T22:17:46.003Z] worker=svc-23 trace=tr-9987 last-kv-prime=0x7f3a
[2026-03-09T22:17:46.004Z] choice-stream: flushed tail fragments but no terminal-envelope written
[2026-03-09T22:18:05.112Z] client reconnected and attempted resume with resume_id=rc-556
[2026-03-09T22:18:05.113Z] resume: snapshot mismatch, refusing resume -> fallback served but terminal metadata absent
[customer-provided] client-js log: "received 3 partial choices, no final event, ws.onclose code=1006"

investigation_notes:
Initial analysis (Support): pattern correlates to external TLS rekey events; connection transitions show half-closed state on server logs.
SRE step: Captured pcap from edge node and confirmed short TCP FIN followed by immediate SYN from same client IP; no backend worker crash seen.
Hypothesis: Proxy-inserted TLS rekey modifies client TCP/TLS state in a way that our edge/keepalive handling treats as half-close and does not queue or persist terminal envelope to resume snapshot. Resume path then rejects resume due to ephemeral snapshot mismatch.
Reproducer: Engineering reproduced by running corporate TLS-inspection appliance (testbox) that forces TLS rekey mid-stream; observed identical symptom in ~4/10 runs.
Edge behavior detail: When FIN arrives while last chunk is buffered but not flushed to persistent stream-snapshot, the server sets session state to HALF_CLOSED and GC probes remove pending terminal metadata after 10s. This window aligns with observed data loss.

proposed_next_steps:
- Short term workaround: advise customer to disable mid-stream TLS rekey/rewrite on corp proxy for inference traffic or mark Redwood endpoints in proxy bypass list.
- Medium term: implement atomic flush of terminal envelope to durable snapshot before transitioning session to HALF_CLOSED; add aggressive snapshot checkpoint on any FIN/close path.
- Add metric/trace to alert when session enters HALF_CLOSED with non-flushed-terminal for >5s.
- Run PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1219 to staging with instrumentation and reproduce under testbox.

resolution_notes:
(Pending) No customer-visible resolution yet. Customer accepted bypass workaround to unblock pipelines; engineering own implementation plan queued.

comments:
2026-03-10 08:12 - Maya Thompson (Support): Opened with customer-provided logs and a minimal repro. Customer says 12% of requests on long-running chats see truncated end.
2026-03-10 09:03 - Ethan Park (SRE): Confirmed logs show FIN before terminal-envelope; collecting pcap from edge-03 for deeper analysis. Posted findings to #support and #sre (link: slack://channels/support).
2026-03-10 11:25 - Lina Gomez (Customer): We ran an immediate test disabling TLS inspection for *.redwood.ai and saw no truncated streams during a 2h window. We'd prefer server-side fix but applying bypass is acceptable short term.
2026-03-11 14:40 - Arun Patel (Infra): Reproducer built with test TLS-inspector box. Reproduced 3/10. Found race where buffer flush wins vs. FIN timing; created PR with checkpoint flush (see related_github_prs).
2026-03-12 10:02 - Ethan Park (SRE): Rolling 'instrumented snapshot' change to staging for soak. Added alert rule to paging when half-closed sessions >5s with pending-terminal. Assigning owner for rollout: @Arun.
2026-03-12 12:30 - Support (Maya): Updated customer that we have a staged patch and recommended bypass until fix is deployed. Customer acknowledged and set proxy bypass for Redwood endpoints.

Ryan — thanks, and apologies for the slightly delayed follow-up. High level: yes, Redwood can offer a tokenized audit-proxy pattern that satisfies the KMS and access-audit constraints. Broad proposal below; happy to iterate.

Summary proposal (ops model)
- Storage: Artifacts encrypted at rest with customer-supplied KMS key (we do not hold unencrypted copies).
- Escrow operator: Trusted third-party storage (AuditWorks) as the physical escrow; encryption and token gating managed by Redwood's control plane inside the customer's VPC or via a private connector for Dedicated customers.

- Audit trail: Immutable event log (append-only) surfaced in Redwood Console plus export to customer SIEM / supplied webhook.
- Retention: default 90 days; can be reduced to 30 days or extended to 365 on contract.
- SLA: access request turnaround: 4 business hours (standard) / 1 business hour (escalated) for on-call support (can be negotiated into Dedicated contracts).

3) Ryan: if OK, we'll route a short DocuSign SOW/NDA to get the legal language in place.

evidence.title: Data Access Certification & Retention Escrow — proposal
evidence.text:
Purpose and context:
This draft proposes a short-form contractual clause and operational runbook for (i) certification of data access events and (ii) a limited retention escrow (evidence escrow) tied to on-prem and private deployments of Redwood inference. Aim is to give customers a bounded way to obtain third-party-verifiable records for compliance/legal needs while minimizing long-term retention risk for Redwood.

Key objectives (design principles):
- Time-boxed: escrowed artifacts are retained only for a narrowly scoped period (default 90 days) unless the customer triggers a preservation request.
- Minimal content: store metadata/transactional logs and redacted payloads rather than full user content unless strictly required and mutually agreed.
- Verifiability: artifacts should be cryptographically stamped and accompanied by a tamper-evident manifest for independent audit.
- Operational controls: well-defined access request, approval workflow, and emergency suspension process.

Definitions (working):
- "Evidence Escrow Vault": a secured storage location (customer-managed S3-compatible or Redwood-hosted sealed store) where preserved artifacts are placed.
- "Certified Access Report (CAR)": a signed package including event metadata, cryptographic checksum(s), access-control snapshot, and operator attestations for a given time window.
- "Retention Window": the default period that artifacts are kept in the Evidence Escrow Vault (proposed: 90 days).
- "Preservation Trigger": an authenticated customer request (legal hold, litigation hold, regulatory inquiry) that extends retention for specified items.

Draft clause (contract language — short form):
1) Escrowed Artifacts. Vendor shall place, for the Retention Window, a copy of the artifacts specified in Schedule A ("Escrowed Artifacts") into the Evidence Escrow Vault. Escrowed Artifacts will be limited to: service logs, index-level metadata, access-control snapshots, and redacted request identifiers. Full request payloads will not be escrowed unless Customer provides written authorization in Schedule A.

2) Retention Window and Preservation. The standard Retention Window is ninety (90) days from time of creation. Customer may issue a Preservation Trigger in writing to extend retention for specific Escrowed Artifacts subject to Section 4 (Fees and access). Any extension will be narrow in scope and include an end date or event that terminates the hold.

3) Certification Package. For any Customer-requested CAR, Vendor will provide a signed Certification Package within ten (10) business days. The package will include: (a) event metadata (timestamps, node/region, request id), (b) a cryptographic digest of the stored artifact, (c) an operator attestation describing the preservation process, and (d) the Evidence Escrow Vault manifest. Vendor’s signature will use key material under Vendor control unless Customer requests use of a mutually trusted signing key (see Schedule B).

4) Access and Audit Rights. Customer’s authorized auditor may inspect CARs and request a one-time on-site or remote verification session. Audit scope must be pre-approved and limited to the specific Escrowed Artifacts identified in the Preservation Trigger. Vendor will not disclose customer-created content beyond redactions agreed in Schedule A without Customer’s written consent or lawful process.

5) Sequestration and Emergency Suspension. If Vendor reasonably suspects unauthorized exfiltration or other compromise, Vendor may: (a) suspend writing new Escrowed Artifacts to the Evidence Escrow Vault, (b) freeze retrieval access pending investigation, and (c) provide interim CARs describing the incident. Vendor will notify Customer within forty-eight (48) hours of reasonable belief of compromise and provide remediation steps and timeline.

6) Fees. Standard retention and CAR generation are included up to [X] CARs/month. Additional preservation requests or extended retention will be charged per Schedule C (operational fees). Fee negotiation points: threshold before fee applies, carveouts for production incidents.

7) Data Minimization and Redaction. Vendor will apply agreed redaction rules (Schedule A) to minimize personal data exposure in escrow. Customer and Vendor will jointly adopt a redaction baseline during onboarding; deviation requires mutual agreement.

8) Termination and Disposal. Upon expiration of the Retention Window (or termination of all preservation holds), Vendor will securely delete Escrowed Artifacts and produce a Proof of Destruction certificate signed by an authorized operator. Proofs will include checksum of the deleted objects and time of deletion.

Operational runbook (practical steps — internal notes):
- Onboarding checklist:
  - Confirm customer choice: customer-managed vault (preferred) vs Redwood-hosted sealed vault.
  - Populate Schedule A (artifact granularity) and Schedule B (signing key options).
  - Capture redaction profile and legal contacts for preservation triggers.
  - Create JIRA ticket with tag SEC-ESCROW onboard-<customer>.

- Preservation request flow:
  1) Customer sends Preservation Trigger to security-escrow@redwood.ai and copies legal@customerdomain.
  2) Escrow owner (security) opens a triage call within 4 business hours.
  3) Security engages infra to snapshot manifest and generate CAR.
  4) Legal assesses scope and confirms fees/hold duration.
  5) Vendor uploads CAR to Evidence Escrow Vault and notifies Customer with retrieval instructions.

- CAR generation checklist (operator):
  - Identify artifact IDs and compute SHA256 digests.
  - Export access-control snapshot (IAM/ACL state) for time window.
  - Record infra node/region and operator steps with timestamps.
  - Apply redaction script to payloads if required and store redaction log.
  - Sign package with escrow-signing key and produce manifest.

Negotiation notes / bargaining chips (internal):
- Customers often push for longer default retention (180-365 days). Push back with: increased cost, increased legal risk, and propose targeted holds instead.
- For high-sensitivity customers, prefer customer-managed vault + customer signing key. This reduces vendor liability and is a strong win for customers but raises onboarding friction.
- Offer tiered pricing: baseline (90d, 3 CARs/mo), premium (180d, 12 CARs/mo), enterprise (custom).

Open questions and TODOs:
- Decide default fee thresholds (e.g., 1 free CAR per 30 days per account? tie to committed spend?) -- ACTION: finance + legal to propose pricing band by 2026-03-01.
- Implementation: do we use separate KMS keys per customer for evidence signing or a multi-tenant signing service? ACTION: infra to prototype customer-key option (JIRA-SEC-234).
- Legal review: add language about lawful process vs. customer consent for disclosure. ACTION: Legal to draft final carveouts by next review.

Quick decision log (history of edits):
- 2025-11-08: initial draft by Ava.
- 2025-12-16: added Preservation Trigger workflow (Marcus).
- 2026-01-10: inserted sequestration notification SLA (Sofia).
- 2026-02-21: updated CAR timeline and retention default (Ethan).

Appendix A — Schedule A (example artifact list, to be customized per customer):
- Service log index entries (timestamp, request id, model id, token count)
- Request metadata (redacted client IP, region, route)
- Access-control snapshot (roles, policies active)
- Redacted payloads only if customer authorizes, with redaction rules enumerated

Appendix B — Example Preservation Trigger template (email):
Subject: Preservation Trigger — [Customer] — Escrow artifacts for [YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD]
Body:
  1) Customer name and account id
  2) Artifact identifiers or selection criteria (time range, request ids, model id)
  3) Intended retention extension and reason (litigation/regulatory/investigation)
  4) Contact/legal POC and signature

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the default retention short; we don't want a proliferation of long-lived evidence stores.
- Make customer-managed vault the recommended default in sales materials — reduces friction on sensitive customers.
- Build a small UI in console to request CARs and track Preservation Triggers (saves ops emails).

Attachment checklist for negotiation:
- Draft Schedule A (per-customer)
- Schedule B: key management options
- Sample CAR (redacted) for customer review
- Pricing bands for retention and CARs

End of draft.

[This doc is a working draft. Comments inline are expected; please use the Confluence page linked above for version tracking.]

evidence.title: eng-platform
evidence.text:
rachael: Heads-up: after the v1->v2 soft-roll last night we got two noise reports: unexpected quota hits and confusing console state. Need quick sync on visibility + a short circuit-breaker in console for auto-flips.

mike: Can you summarise what tenants saw? Was it billing, throttles, or both?

rachael: Mix. Mostly bursty quota errors for tenants with heavy short requests, plus a few support tickets where console still showed "v1" even though routing flipped.

zubin: That sounds like a race between route table update and console cache invalidation. We currently invalidate console cache on route-change event but the event is async and can lag ~10-30s.

infra-bot: deploy: rollout v2-auto-flip to 20% completed at 2025-12-05T02:10:12Z.

mike: Two proposals: 1) show "migration pending" state in console immediately when we schedule a flip, and 2) add an emergency circuit-breaker toggle that pauses auto-flips per-tenant.

harry: For telemetry we should emit `migration_state` (scheduled/pending/active/complete) and `migration_reason` (console/manual/autoswitch). That lets ops filter any anomalies tied to how the flip was initiated.

mica: UX: add an inline banner on tenant page: "Migration scheduled (click to pause). Estimated warmup: 3m. View details -> ". Keep CTA small.

rachael: Ops asked for a per-tenant quick revert button in the console that only flips routing back and sets a tagging flag so we can audit. Not full rollback, just quick revert.

zubin: Backend: revert button -> create route change event with origin=console_revert and `revert_marker=true`. Telemetry will capture it. Need to ensure we don't create oscillations. Add a cooldown flag for 10m per tenant.

mike: Quota issue: tenants triggered rate-limit because many clients retried after transient 429s during warmup. Two mitigations: token-saver mode (cap max seq-len) and client-facing header `X-Migration-Suggested-Backoff`. We can also add a short TTL on throttle counters during migration to avoid double-counting retries.

harry: I'd rather avoid changing throttle semantics broadly. Suggest adding a migration-aware throttle window: maintain a separate `migration_retry_bucket` that decays faster. That prevents retry storms from inflating normal quota metrics.

mica: Console copy for circuit-breaker: "Pause automatic migrations for this tenant. Use when you see unexpected cost or throttles. Pausing will keep current model routing until you resume." Include a secondary action "Safe-canary 5%" so users can opt to only migrate a slice.

zubin: Telemetry specifics: emit counters every 30s: `tenant.migration.tokens.30s`, `tenant.migration.fallback_tokens.30s`, `tenant.migration.kv_miss_rate.30s`, and a boolean `tenant.migration.paused`. Keep labels low-cardinality: tenant_id, migration_state, route_origin. Sample raw traces at 1% by default, 10% during the first 5 minutes after schedule.

rachael: Good. Also please add a console endpoint `GET /tenants/{id}/migration/preview` that returns estimated $ impact and suggested mitigation (cap seq-len, safe-canary) before we flip. Help CS answer questions.

mike: We should also add an internal alert: if `migration.fallback_tokens.1m` > 40% and `migration.kv_miss_rate.1m` > 0.2 concurrently, page oncall and create an incident note prefilled with affected tenant and last 15 min graph links.

billing-bot: billing-note: default billing policy remains "bill for model served". Any temporary grace/refund policy requires Legal sign-off; you can add a "simulate_billing=true" mode for canaries so we record but don't charge.

harry: For console state lag we can also add optimistic UI update: set UI to pending state as soon as the flip is scheduled and update to final when event confirmed. That reduces confusion.

mica: Agree. UX must show an explicit timestamp and "last updated by" so customers see who triggered the flip.

rachael: Action list: zubin -> route_event + revert/cooldown + migration telemetry; harry -> alert rules; mica -> console pill + revert + safe-canary action + optimistic UI; mike -> throttle migration bucket + token-saver feature; billing-bot/legal -> simulate_billing mode guidance.

zubin: I'll PR the route event changes and add the 30s aggregated counters. Can someone own the endpoint for migration/preview?

mike: I'll take migration/preview API and the token-saver enforcement.

mike: Quickie: sample SQL for the preview aggregator (will run in metrics infra):

```
SELECT
  tenant_id,
  sum(tokens) FILTER (WHERE migration_state='active') AS migration_tokens,
  sum(tokens) FILTER (WHERE migration_state='steady') AS baseline_tokens,
  (sum(tokens) FILTER (WHERE migration_state='active') - sum(tokens) FILTER (WHERE migration_state='steady')) AS token_delta
FROM request_metrics
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '10 minutes'
GROUP BY tenant_id
LIMIT 100;
```

harry: I'll draft alert runbook and page template. We'll include recommended mitigations and a link to quick revert in console.

mica: I'll post mocks in #design later today. Keep language low-friction.

rachael: Thanks everyone. If no objections, let's aim to ship the telemetry + optimistic UI + circuit-breaker to canary tenants by next Wednesday. Add blockers as replies. :thumbsup:

evidence.title: Hosted API: implement failure grace-window + customer fast-path to contain retry storms during escalations
evidence.text:
description:
Summary: Multiple customers escalated after observing cascading 5xx/timeouts during transient upstream slowdowns. Symptoms included synchronized client retries, spike in outgoing RPC latency, and frontdoor connection pileup. This ticket implements a short 'grace-window' circuit policy and a per-tenant fast-path guard to reduce retry amplification and preserve capacity for prioritized customer bridges during live escalations.

Context & impact: Over the last month several incident postmortems pointed to short-lived backend slowdowns that generated a wave of client retries. Our existing circuit-breakers tripped too quickly for some flows or too late for others; once tripped, fallbacks triggered heavy routing changes that increased tail latency and produced customer-visible 502/504 errors. Customers in P1 escalations need a temporary 'fast-path' that reduces their effective admission checks and prevents them from being swept up in tenant-wide backoffs while we remediate root causes.

Goals: 1) reduce retry amplification during short upstream slowdowns, 2) provide an on-call-safe escape-hatch to steer specific customer traffic to a prioritized admission lane, 3) increase observability so SREs/SEs can make informed in-incident decisions without code changes.

Proposed approach: Implement a multi-part change: (A) Grace-window circuit-breaker semantics: instead of immediately increasing circuit score on the first N failures, apply a 10s sliding grace window that counts only sustained error rates above threshold before tripping. This permits transient spikes to recover without hard-routing changes. (B) Retry-suppression token: attach a short-lived header (X-RW-Retry-Suppress) for internal gateways to suppress client-side hedged retries when we detect amplification patterns. (C) Customer fast-path flagging: add an admission router flag that temporarily lowers queueing thresholds for flagged tenant IDs and routes them to a small warm pool reserved for escalations. (D) Observability/UI: Console endpoint with per-tenant 'escalation mode' marker and a dashboard panel showing grace-window triggers, suppressed retries, and fast-path occupancy.

Root cause hypothesis: client retry storms + synchronous admission policies amplified transient backend latency into service-wide 5xx waves. Existing mechanisms either over-react (trip too quickly) or under-protect high-priority customers.

Trade-offs considered: 1) Longer grace windows reduce false-positive trips but increase the time before we isolate a legitimately failing backend. We chose a conservative 10s default with per-route tunables. 2) Fast-path reduces latency for flagged customers but increases isolation risk; the pool size is intentionally small and subject to autoscaling guardrails. 3) Retry-suppression requires changes across edge and SDKs; we implement suppression opportunistically at our gateways first and later expose SDK guidance.

Progress updates:
- 2026-02-13: Spike implementation and prototype circuit-window logic completed (Arjun). Local integration tests show reduced trip rate on synthetic jittered error traces.
- 2026-02-15: Design review with SRE and Product (notes attached). Decided to use header-based suppression to avoid client SDK changes in the hot path (SRE signoff: Diego Rivera).
- 2026-02-17: PR #4982 opened for admission-router changes and new grace-window circuit state machine (PR link below).
- 2026-02-19: End-to-end staging run with 3 tenants simulating retry storms. Fast-path prevented two tenants from being impacted while non-flagged tenants experienced isolated degradation. Observability panels validated.
- 2026-02-22: Security review: no encryption or KMS changes needed. Security requested audit logs for any fast-path toggles (added).
- 2026-02-24: Canaries ready for controlled rollout to prod-1 region. Preparing runbook and customer communication templates.

Testing plan: unit tests for circuit logic, integration harness with synthetic client retry driver, staging soak with tenant-weighted load, and dark launch of X-RW-Retry-Suppress header on 1% of traffic. Acceptance criteria below.

Rollout plan: 1) Dark launch grace-window in runtime-1.24 canary with telemetry only. 2) Enable retry-suppression header handling in gateways and log toggles. 3) Enable per-tenant fast-path behind feature flag; reserve pool at 2% capacity initially. 4) Runbook: SREs may toggle fast-path for customer on-call; toggles recorded in audit logs. 5) If any regressions, roll back feature flag and revert admission-router configuration.

Customer comms: Draft saved for customer-bridge teams. Template includes symptom explanation, mitigation steps we performed, and a recommended client SDK update timeline for retry-suppression semantics.

Post-incident actions: update SDK docs with recommended retry jitter/backoff patterns, instrument more granular per-route latency percentiles, and create a retrospective for improving route-level defaults.

acceptance_criteria:
Grace-window circuit prevents at least 70% of transient trips in staged test workload without increasing sustained error exposure
Retry-suppression header propagated and honored by gateway; suppression events appear in logs and dashboard
Console shows per-tenant escalation mode and fast-path pool occupancy; SREs can toggle per-tenant flag via UI
Feature flag rollout tested in prod-1 canary for 48 hours with no elevated 5xx rate attributable to the change
Audit log entries recorded for all fast-path toggles during rollout

decisions:
Use 10s default grace-window with per-route override rather than global 30s window
Implement retry-suppression via internal header first to avoid SDK rollouts during initial mitigation
Reserve small (2-5%) warm pool capacity per-region for fast-path rather than unbounded routing priority
Require audit logging for fast-path toggles before rollout to all regions

notes:
SRE recommended additional tracing tags for correlated retry chains (trace.parent_retry_id)
Product requested we expose a read-only escalation status API for customer success teams
Design and Console teams suggested a simple 'Escalation' badge on the tenant dashboard to avoid runbook navigation during incidents

elaine: yes. oscillation was painful last month. hysteresis + minimum duration seems necessary. also want a clear sampling audit so we can replay decisions.

evidence.title: Slots eviction arbitration and model-variant rollback strategy for hosted spillover
evidence.text:
description:
Implement an arbitration and rollback playbook that governs how requests are moved from Dedicated capacity to Hosted during short-term pressure and how we demote/promote model variants without violating tenant SLOs. This ticket captures the algorithm, operational runbook, metrics, and automated gates for: (1) slot eviction arbitration in dedicated pools, (2) admission/circuit-breaker thresholds for hosted spillover, (3) variant rollback criteria when quality regressions or latency spikes are detected, and (4) a staged rollout with canaries and emergency rollback paths.

acceptance_criteria:
Eviction arbitration algorithm implemented and covered by unit and integration tests (simulated multi-tenant pressure).
Automated circuit-breaker that prevents >X% of a tenant's traffic spilling to hosted within a sliding 5-minute window (configurable).
Variant rollback triggers defined: p99 latency > latency_threshold OR generation-quality drop > quality_threshold on evaluation set for two consecutive minutes.
Runbook documented and exercised in staging with a scheduled chaos test that simulates a transient 30% capacity loss in a dedicated pool.
Dashboard: per-tenant spill rate, spill latency delta, model-variant assignment, eviction events and reason codes instrumented in Console.

design_decisions:
Use a soft-eviction lane: instead of immediate preemption, mark a subset of slots as ‘evictable’ and gracefully finish in-flight requests up to a 2s drain window to avoid high tail latencies.
Prioritize eviction candidates by a composite score: tenant SLA tier weight, historical spill frequency (cooldown), and active in-flight token count. This balances fairness and predictability.
Cap hosted spill proportion per customer via a token-bucket like allowance to limit sudden cross-tenant spikes and protect hosted capacity for public users.
Rollback decisions for model variants are based on a small, tenant-specific eval set run in shadow mode and combined signal (latency + quality + error-rate). Each signal has configurable weight and hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping.
Expose runtime knobs in Console (per-tenant soft-reserve %, spill cap, eviction grace ms, rollback hysteresis minutes) and surface recommended defaults derived from production telemetry.

tradeoffs:
Aggressive eviction reduces queueing on dedicated GPUs but may increase total tokens billed on hosted; choosing defaults balances latency SLO vs cost.
Longer drain windows reduce p99 spikes but risk delaying eviction under severe capacity loss; 2s chosen as compromise after staging tests.
Per-tenant eval sets improve rollback signal quality but add overhead in telemetry and require maintenance; we will start with a shared canonical eval + top-10 tenant custom sets.
Hard caps on spillover protect hosted customers but can cause increased throttling for large enterprise tenants; we provide override flows for emergency capacity expansions.

rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (staging): implement arbitration algorithm behind a feature flag; run chaos job (simulate 30% dedicated loss) and verify no outage and runbook steps succeed.
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5 low-risk tenants in us-west-2 dedicated pools; monitor spill rate, p95/p99 latency, and hosted saturation for 48h.
Phase 2 (ramped): 25% of tenants with dedicated in a region; enable per-tenant spill caps and observe operator alerts and automatic rollback behavior for 7 days.
Phase 3 (global): enable by default with Console defaults and allow customers to opt-out or request dedicated reserve adjustments; document emergency increase protocol with SRE and Sales.

test_plan:
Unit tests for eviction scoring, tie-breakers, and grace window enforcement.
Integration test: multi-tenant simulator that injects request bursts and verifies spill caps, eviction ordering, and no tenant exceeds spill allowance.
Chaos test in staging: periodic GPU node drain during business hours to validate automatic arbitration and runbook procedures.
Quality regression test: run tenant-specific evals in shadow against promoted variants and ensure rollback triggers fire when quality falls below baseline by configured delta.
Load test: verify hosted circuit-breaker prevents >20% capacity saturation from a single tenant under burst conditions.

comments:
2026-03-02 Marco Nguyen: Initial prototype of the scoring function (PR linked). Observed small unfairness against small tenants in synthetic runs; added cooldown factor to scoring.
2026-03-05 SRE - Lina Gomez: Confirmed alert thresholds; suggested adding operator-initiated soft-reserve bump to avoid paging during business-critical migrations.
2026-03-08 Product - Rajiv Menon: Requested UI controls for per-tenant spill caps and a tooltip explaining billing implications.
2026-03-10 Design - Claire Zhou: Reviewed Console mockups; recommended default values and placement for the rollback hysteresis control.
2026-03-12 QA - Omar Hassan: Completed integration test harness; failure mode found where multiple simultaneous evictions caused transient host saturation — mitigating change pushed to branch.
2026-03-13 Aisha Patel: Merged change to adjust drain window to 2s; scheduled staging chaos test for 2026-03-18.

next_steps:
Finish PR reviews and merge runtime changes behind feature flag (owner: Marco).
Complete staging chaos test and capture metrics (owner: SRE).
Implement Console UI knobs and add documentation for Sales and Support on opt-outs and emergency capacity requests.
Schedule runbook tabletop with SRE, Support, Sales to validate escalation and billing messaging before canary.

evidence.title: docs
evidence.text:
Lina: FYI I ran the site build on the mkdocs preview and linkcheck flagged a bunch of anchors that look valid in the source but 404 on the generated pages. Example: a header `Mount cache (TTL)` -> anchor became `mount-cache-ttl` in the HTML but some internal refs still target `mount_cache_ttl`.
Sam: Oof. That smells like mixed slugify rules between the migration transform and mkdocs config. Did the converter apply a different slugifier than mkdocs-material?

Marc: It did. The mdx->md step used a JS slugify with underscore fallback for numbers. MkDocs is using python-slugify with default separator='-'. They diverge on spaces + punctuation.
Tess: Quick check: grep for anchors referenced with underscores: `rg "#.*_.*_.*\)" docs | head` — found ~18 hits across guides and integrations.
Priya: We should do two things: 1) patch mkdocs to mimic the old slug rules to stop new breakage, 2) generate redirect entries for the already-broken fragment variants so inbound links don't 404.
Mae: Agreed. I prototyped a small mkdocs plugin in infra/docs-plugins that sets slugify(separator='-') and ascii transliteration= True. Locally it made the anchors match the preview site for several pages.
Lina: Good. For redirects, can we auto-generate both dashed and underscored variants for every heading? That should cover most mismatches.
Sam: Yes; I wrote a quick script `scripts/fragment_redirects.py` that parses each .md, extracts headings and emits YAML entries mapping both variants to the canonical anchor. It also skips headings that contain inline code or emoji to avoid noisy redirects.
Tess: A couple of gotchas: headings inside includes ({{ include('...') }}) were being deduped differently by the converter, so the same heading slug can appear on multiple pages. The redirect script needs to key with page path + fragment.
Priya: I'll open PR #4210 with the redirect generator plus tests. It's set to produce data/fragment-redirects.yaml and a tiny unit test that ensures for each heading both `-` and `_` forms exist.
Marc: We also should add a docs-ci check to detect empty-language code fences — those broken fences break copy buttons. Another migration-side bug I found was untagged fences like:

```
console.log("hi")
```

which need `js` or `python` tags.
Lina: Right — that was tripping highlight.js. Can we heuristically re-tag fences if empty? Sam, maybe your snippet detector can do that.
Sam: Yep. I'll add detection: look at the first non-blank line in fence; if it starts with `def|import|from|class` -> python, `function|const|import` -> js, shebang or `#!/bin/bash` -> bash. I'll add a `--dry-run` mode to print candidates.
Mae: Also note inline HTML wrappers like `<div class="example">```js` prevented markdown parsers from recognising the fence entirely. The fixer should unwrap these before tagging.
Tess: I'll include an HTML strip step in the script. For safety, the script will output a patch but not auto-commit; we can review in PR. PTAL @sam @marc.
Priya: PRs are linked: #4210 (fragment redirects), #4211 (fence retagger script), #4212 (mkdocs-plugin slugify change). I've added reviewers and test CI.
Deploy-bot: docs-ci job 10322 queued
Deploy-bot: docs-ci job 10322 failed  linkcheck reported 5 remaining broken fragments
Lina: Which ones remain? Can we get a short list from the job artifacts?
Deploy-bot: artifact: linkcheck/failures.txt (5 entries)
- /guides/ops#mount_cache_ttl -> target not found
- /guides/sdk/python#client-reconnect -> target not found
- /integrations/partner#oauth-20 -> target not found
- /guides/embedding#cache-ttl -> target not found
- /api/streams#stream_reconnect -> target not found
Sam: Two are underscore variants, one is oauth-20 vs oauth-2-0, and client-reconnect looks like a heading inside an include that wasn't generated. I'll add those to the redirect list quickly.
Tess: I've updated PR #4210 with the five fragments and a failing test that mirrors the linkcheck output so CI will only pass once they're in the map.
Deploy-bot: docs-ci job 10329 queued
Deploy-bot: docs-ci job 10329 succeeded
Priya: Green. We should also add a small migration note in docs/migration_notes.md about slugify parity, fence language preservation, and avoiding inline HTML wrappers around fences.
Marc: Agreed. I'll add that and a checklist item: run `scripts/validate_fragments.py` post-migration to detect mismatches before release.
Lina: Sounds good. After merge let's run a GA-driven smoke check list for top 50 inbound urls and confirm no external 404s. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

evidence.text: Maya Patel: FYI the docs CI is failing with a ton of broken fragment errors after the recent headings rename in the runtime guide. build log shows 'Broken fragment: #using-the-runtime' and similar for several pages. Jordan Lee: ugh. Is it the new slugify behavior or a migration mismatch from the old anchors? question: In the mid-March 2026 eu-west canary rollout where sticky fallback kept pinning requests back onto the failing canary instead of the stable quantized variant, what configuration mistake caused the loop and what mitigations were applied to stop it?

evidence.text:
incident-bot: Pager alert: High error rate on rollout policy 'policy-v3' canary. 500s and increased tail latency observed; automatic fallback active. impact: ~5% of requests -> eu-region-variant-b. link: https://redwood.in/alerts/1918007654 :rotating_light:

maria-g: ack. paging @ryan-oncall. tagging eng-runtime and sre. any quick read on customer impact?

aj: looking at the ingress logs now. seeing a spike in grpc errors from routing service at 03:42 UTC. sample: `2026-03-15T03:42:10Z ERROR routepicker: failed to select target: variant-mismatch`

ryan-oncall: i'm oncall and seeing the page. give me a minute to pull traces. what did the canary weight look like?

eli-sre: canary weight was 8% with fallback policy: `sticky: true, fallback_variant: eu-variant-b, max_fallback_duration: 30m`. suspecting sticky fallback + region routing caused a sticky route to a variant that fails under load.

kim-runtime: confirming — the rollout config for policy-v3 shows sticky fallback enabled to preserve session affinity. here's the snippet from the rollout manifest:

```yaml
rollout:
  name: policy-v3
  canary: 8%
  fallback:
    type: variant
    variant: "eu-variant-b"
    sticky: true
    sticky_ttl: 1800s
```

maria-g: customer impact check? which customers hit the failing path?

aj: cross-referencing traces with billing ids. two customers show elevated 500s and degraded SLA: AcmeApps (eu-billing) and FathomAnalytics. both are heavy in EU-REGION. approximate failed requests: 1.2k in last 5m.

ryan-oncall: thanks. i'm going to pause the canary rollout and disable sticky fallback to stop stateful stickiness into the bad variant. can someone confirm rollback / pause command?

deploy-bot: Received command: `rollback policy-v3 --type=canary --confirm`. Executing staged pause...

kim-runtime: before rollback, quick mitigation: set fallback.sticky=false for policy-v3 via feature toggle. command: `rwctl policy update policy-v3 --fallback.sticky=false`

eli-sre: that sounds safer — non-sticky fallback will allow routing to pick a healthy variant instead of forcing traf to the failing EU variant. we still need to pause the canary to stop more users being routed to it.

ryan-oncall: running both: pausing canary + flip fallback. i'll run the rwctl commands now.

ryan-oncall: `rwctl rollout pause policy-v3` -> accepted.

ryan-oncall: `rwctl policy update policy-v3 --fallback.sticky=false` -> accepted.

incident-bot: Action log: rollout paused by ryan-oncall at 03:45 UTC. policy updated: fallback.sticky=false by ryan-oncall.

maria-g: monitoring metrics — can someone post the error rate and p95?

aj: graphs: error rate dropped from 6.8% to 1.1% over 4m after changes. p95 latency for EU requests decreased from 720ms to 210ms.

samantha-pm: notifying affected accounts (AcmeApps, FathomAnalytics) via standard incident template. they were seeing failed completions; ops outreach in progress.

kim-runtime: still want to investigate root cause: why did eu-variant-b fail under canary weight? looks like eu-variant-b has a model binary mismatch against the serving runtime here (kv-cache schema mismatch). logs: `kv_cache: incompatible-kv-schema v2 vs v1` on startup of variant. perhaps model package wasn't validated for that runtime build.

eli-sre: good catch. that explains 500s on requests that hit the variant. also explains why sticky made it worse — sticky kept users bound to that bad variant.

maria-g: next steps: 1) rollback canary (we paused), 2) disable sticky fallback (done), 3) upgrade eu-variant-b packaging with runtime-compatible model binary, 4) add pre-serve validation to prevent variant with kv-schema mismatch from receiving traffic. assign owners?

kim-runtime: i'll own the packaging fix and pre-serve validator. target hotfix in next 2 hours, will post progress.

aj: i'll run a sweep to find other rollout manifests that have sticky fallback enabled and flag them for review (script: `scripts/find_sticky_fallbacks.sh | xargs -n1 echo`).

ryan-oncall: leaving final checks to oncall follow-up. i'll hand to eli-sre for post-incident and to kim for runtime fix.

eli-sre: i'll open an incident ticket and schedule the blameless postmortem. initial impact: two paying customers saw errors for ~12 minutes; internal metric alert threshold tripped. severity: Sev2.

maria-g: thanks everyone. please add timeline and links to logs in the incident ticket.

deploy-bot: Completed: rollback paused, feature toggle applied. no further automated rollouts will run for policy-v3 until manual resume.

kim-runtime: quick note — recommend changing default fallback.sticky to false in rollout templates unless affinity is explicitly required. will put up a PR.

eli-sre: agreed. adding alerting rule: if fallback.sticky=true and variant has serving errors > 1% for 5m -> auto-disable sticky and notify oncall. will draft alert.

samantha-pm: customer comms draft shared in #customer-success for review.

maria-g: closing loop: error rate stable, customers contacted, owners assigned. will keep thread open until runtime fix deployed. :white_check_mark:

jen: ack. I'll standby — can take handoff in ~10m if needed. what's scope: how many customers / percent traffic?

alex: early telemetry: 3 enterprise tenants (custA, custB, custC) with ~10-30% error rates on inference calls. affected traffic ~2% of global, concentrated in EU.

maria: runbook immediate actions: (1) pause the rollout (2) disable sticky fallback for this policy. proposing to execute both unless objections.

sam: concur. alternative is to scale the canary pool to avoid OOMs but pausing and rolling back is safer for now.

jen: executing mitigations now:
```
# pause rollout
redwoodctl rollout pause --id checkout-rewrite-canary
# remove sticky fallback from the routing policy
redwoodctl routing update --policy checkout-policy --remove-fallback sticky
# pin affected tenants to stable region eu-central-1
redwoodctl routing set-region --policy checkout-policy --force eu-central-1 --selector "tenant in (custA,custB,custC)"
```

incident-bot: Action logs: rollout pause submitted by jen at 1972103470; routing update submitted.

sam: confirmed rollout paused, sticky fallback flag cleared, region pinning applied for custA/custB/custC. monitoring for oscillation stop.

alex: notifying support/CS for customer comms. @luis can you draft a short customer notification?

maria: telemetry update ~2 minutes post-mitigation: error rates for custA/B/C down from ~20% to ~1.5%; global metrics back to baseline.

redis-cli -h routing-cache.prod --eval scripts/clear_affinity.lua "checkout-policy" "custA,custB,custC"
```

sam: cache cleared. router logs no longer show cross-region handoffs. latency and success rates returning to normal.

alex: infra side: do we have OOM traces or model load failures to file an ops bug?

maria: opening follow-up task: INF-4921 "canary v2 memory underestimate -> sticky-fallback oscillation" assigned to eng-runtime.

jen: incident summary for pager.go:
- root cause: model variant v2 exceeded memory under specific request distribution in eu-west-1, causing canary health to degrade.
- contributing: smart-routing policy used sticky fallback + region-fallback rules that permitted oscillation between regions.
- mitigations: paused the rollout, removed sticky fallback, pinned affected tenants to stable region, cleared affinity cache, rolled back where necessary.

evidence.title: Interactive Latency Canvas — model/route timelines and streaming vs blocking decomposition
evidence.text:
description:
Background:
We need a single exploratory dashboard (the "Interactive Latency Canvas") that lets SREs, runtime and product owners compare latency distributions across models and routes with automatic separation between streaming vs blocking (non-streaming) IO modes. Existing dashboards are numerous but fragmented; this work consolidates cohorting, trace hooks, and enriched metrics into a unified surface that supports root-cause drills and runbook actions.

Goals:
- Surface p50/p95/p99 latency by model_version and route_name with a toggle for streaming vs blocking IO.
- Allow cohort-based comparisons (prompt length, open/closed loop, kv-cache hit/miss) and request-shape bucketing (short/medium/long).
- Overlay KV-cache hit-rate, batch-size distribution and 'stream-early-output' metric to explain downstream latency variance.
- Link directly to pre-sampled traces that include kernel selection, batch_id, and early-output anchors.
- Provide alerting recipes for streaming-mode regressions (spike in p95 or increase in chunk-latency).

Design & instrumentation changes required:
- Tracing: add trace attributes: model_version, route_name, io_mode (streaming|blocking), batch_id, kernel_variant, kv_cache_hit (true|false), response_first_chunk_ts. Update trace hook to capture first-chunk timestamp for streaming flows.
- Metrics: enrich latency timer metrics with tags: model_version, route_name, io_mode, prompt_len_bucket, kv_cache_hit. Emit histogram buckets suitable for p50/p95/p99 calculation.
- Logs: surface error_code and internal_fallback flags per request; forward to logs pipeline with same enrichment tags.
- Metrics/log pipeline: ensure enrichment occurs in the metrics agent before aggregation and that the metrics backend stores per-model/route series (avoid cardinality explosion by using prompt_len_bucket).

Dashboard components (interactive):
1) Top-line selector: model_version, route_name, time window, compare axis (left/right).
2) Latency skyline: stacked percentiles (p50/p95/p99) over time with shading for streaming vs blocking. Clicking a percentile drills to the cohort table.
3) Cohort panel: single-click cohorts by prompt_len_bucket, kv_cache_hit, request_shape, and client_region with sparklines.
4) Batch/Kernel overlay: histogram of batch sizes and kernel_variant frequency correlated to latency spikes.
5) Streaming chunk inspector: distribution of response_first_chunk_latency and subsequent chunk inter-arrival latencies.
6) Trace link column: sampled trace IDs with reason tags (high p99, kv miss, fallback).
7) SLO heatmap: per-model/route p95 breach frequency and recent incidents.

Acceptance criteria (definition of done):
- Dashboard deployed in staging with live data for at least 48 hours and accurate p50/p95/p99 breakdowns for streaming and blocking modes.
- Trace hooks emit the new attributes and the trace link opens to a trace that includes kernel_variant and response_first_chunk_ts.
- Metrics enrichment is in place for model_version and route_name without unbounded cardinality; queries for p50/p95/p99 are efficient (< 5s for 1h window).
- Cohort filters correctly subset series and re-compute percentiles; KV-cache overlay aligns with latency spikes.
- Alerting rule for streaming-mode p95 increase is added with paging policy and runbook link.
- PR and design doc reviewed by Observability and Runtime teams and QA runbook created.

Implementation notes / queries for reviewers:
- Suggest storing prompt_len_bucket at source (agent) with buckets: short(<64), medium(64-512), long(>512) to limit cardinality.
- For streaming traces we need to decide sampling policy: 1% baseline + 100% for requests with p99 > threshold. Does SRE approve temporary higher sampling during rollout?
- Consider pre-computing p95/p99 in metrics ingest layer for common model/route combinations to keep query latency low.

Rollout plan:
1) Instrumentation PRs (tracing + metrics agent) -> staging smoke test -> metric cardinality sanity run.
2) Dashboard initial UAT with Runtime/Observability -> tweak cohorts.
3) Enable in prod read-only for 1 week, then open edit and alerts.
4) Postmortem after 2 weeks to capture false positives and tuning.

Notes for follow-up tickets:
- Follow-up: add model-compare mode to overlay two models on same route (separate ticket).
- Follow-up: per-customer (org) breakdown for Dedicated customers with private metrics routing.

evidence.title: Interactive Latency Canvas — Design & Instrumentation Guide (Model/Route timelines + Streaming vs Blocking)
evidence.text:
## Overview
The Interactive Latency Canvas is a single exploratory dashboard that allows SREs, Runtime, and product owners to compare latency distributions across **models** and **routes**, with an explicit decomposition between **streaming** and **blocking** (non-streaming) response modes.

This page is the implementation guide for:
- Required **metrics + trace attributes**
- Cardinality controls (what we will/won’t tag)
- Dashboard panel requirements
- Alerting recipes and validation steps

## Goals
1. Surface p50/p95/p99 latency by **model_version** and **route_name**, with a toggle for **io_mode = streaming|blocking**.
2. Enable cohort-based comparisons:
   - prompt length bucket (token-based)
   - request shape bucket (short/medium/long *completion length*)
   - KV-cache hit/miss
   - client_region
3. Provide explanatory overlays:
   - KV-cache hit rate
   - batch size distribution
   - stream “first token” latency
   - kernel variant selection frequency
4. Link directly to pre-sampled traces (high p99, KV-miss, fallback) for root-cause drilldown.
5. Provide alerting templates for **streaming regressions** (p95/p99) and **first-token latency** regressions.

## Non-goals (explicitly out of scope)
- Per-customer/org breakdown in the default dashboard (Dedicated customers may require private metrics routing).
- Unbounded per-request dimensions (prompt hash, request id, user id, etc.).

---

## Instrumentation Requirements
### Required dimensions (tags)
All latency and first-token timing metrics MUST include the following tags:
- `model_version` (string, e.g., `llama3.1-70b-instruct@2026-03-07`)
- `route_name` (string, e.g., `chat.completions`)
- `io_mode` (`streaming` | `blocking`)
- `prompt_len_bucket` (token-based buckets; see below)
- `kv_cache_hit` (`true` | `false` | `unknown`)

Recommended additional tags where available:
- `client_region` (coarse: `na`, `eu`, `apac`, `sa`, `unknown`)
- `request_shape` (coarse: `short`, `medium`, `long`, `unknown`)

### Prompt length buckets (UPDATED)
To reduce cardinality and align with token-based capacity planning, prompt length buckets are defined in **tokens** (not characters):
- `short`: `<128`
- `medium`: `128–1024`
- `long`: `>1024`

Rationale: earlier char-based buckets produced inconsistent cohorting across tokenizers and languages.

### Metrics (canonical names)
The following metric names are the standard expected by the dashboard queries. If a service uses alternate names, add a translation layer in the metrics agent.

**Latency histograms**
- `inference.request_latency_ms` (histogram)
  - Definition: end-to-end request latency from request acceptance to final response completion.
  - Tags: required tags above.

**Streaming first-token timing (UPDATED field name)**
- `inference.first_token_latency_ms` (histogram)
  - Definition: for streaming only, time from request acceptance to first token emitted.
  - Tags: required tags above.

**Chunk inter-arrival (optional, streaming only)**
- `inference.stream_chunk_gap_ms` (histogram)
  - Definition: time between consecutive chunks (or token batches) emitted.
  - Tags: `model_version`, `route_name`, `io_mode=streaming`, `prompt_len_bucket`.

**KV cache**
- `inference.kv_cache_hit_total` (counter)
- `inference.kv_cache_req_total` (counter)

**Batching**
- `inference.batch_size` (histogram)
  - Tag: `kernel_variant` is allowed on this metric only if the allowed set is enumerated and stable.

### Tracing attributes
Traces should contain the following attributes to support drilldown from the dashboard:
- `model_version`
- `route_name`
- `io_mode` (`streaming` | `blocking`)
- `batch_id` (string or int; may be absent if not batched)
- `kernel_variant` (string; constrained set)
- `kv_cache_hit` (`true`|`false`|`unknown`)
- `first_token_ts` (timestamp; streaming only) **(UPDATED: replaces `response_first_chunk_ts`)**
- `internal_fallback` (`true`|`false`)
- `error_code` (string; e.g., `timeout`, `oom`, `upstream_429`, `unknown`)

**Note:** For legacy compatibility, services may emit both `response_first_chunk_ts` and `first_token_ts` during migration. The dashboard assumes `first_token_ts` when present.

### Sampling policy (UPDATED)
During rollout, use a stable baseline plus triggered escalation:
- Baseline: **1%** trace sampling
- Triggered: **100% sampling** for 15 minutes when any of the following conditions are met per (model_version, route_name, io_mode):
  - p99 `inference.request_latency_ms` exceeds 2× the 7-day median, OR
  - p95 `inference.first_token_latency_ms` exceeds 1.5× the 7-day median (streaming only), OR
  - `error_code` rate exceeds 2%.

SRE guidance: avoid a fixed 2% baseline unless incident-driven; use triggered sampling to manage cost.

---

## Cardinality Controls (must-follow)
1. Do NOT tag metrics with:
   - raw prompt length (numeric)
   - request id / trace id
   - customer org id (default pipeline)
   - model prompt template id
2. `route_name` must be a low-cardinality identifier (canonical route), not full URL paths.
3. `kernel_variant` must not be attached to the main request latency histogram unless the number of variants is tightly bounded and reviewed.
4. Enrichment must happen in the **metrics agent before aggregation**, and dashboards must query using the standardized buckets.

Target guardrail: total series growth attributable to this work should be **<15%** in the primary metrics backend for Serving + Gateway.

---

## Dashboard Specification (Interactive Latency Canvas)
### 1) Top-line selector
Controls:
- model_version
- route_name
- time window
- io_mode toggle: streaming / blocking / both
- compare axis (A vs B) for cohorts or model versions

### 2) Latency skyline panel
- Chart: p50/p95/p99 over time
- Ability to overlay streaming vs blocking (stacked shading or side-by-side)
- Click-to-drill: selecting a time region filters downstream panels

### 3) Cohort panel
Single-click cohorts with sparklines:
- prompt_len_bucket
- kv_cache_hit
- request_shape
- client_region

### 4) Batch/Kernel overlay
- Batch size histogram overlaid with p95/p99 spikes
- Kernel variant frequency (top N) shown as a time series or stacked area

### 5) Streaming inspector
Streaming-only panels:
- `first_token_latency_ms` p50/p95/p99
- `stream_chunk_gap_ms` distribution (optional where available)

### 6) Trace links table
A table of sampled traces including “reason tags”:
- high p99
- kv miss
- fallback
- elevated first-token latency

### 7) SLO heatmap
Per model/route p95 breach frequency:
- windowed by 1h / 6h / 24h
- includes links to recent incident tickets and runbooks

---

## Alerting Recipes
### Streaming p95 regression (recommended)
Signal:
- Metric: `inference.request_latency_ms` p95 where `io_mode=streaming`
- Condition: p95 > **1.25×** 7-day median for **10 minutes**
- Group by: `model_version`, `route_name`

Routing:
- Page if `customer_impact=high` model/route list; otherwise create ticket.

Runbook link:
- confluence://eng-sre/Runbook+Streaming+Latency+Regression

### First-token latency regression (streaming)
- Metric: `inference.first_token_latency_ms` p95
- Condition: p95 > **1.5×** 7-day median for **10 minutes**
- Add diagnostic links to:
  - KV hit-rate
  - batch size histogram
  - kernel variant frequency

### Blocking mode tail regression
- Metric: `inference.request_latency_ms` p99 where `io_mode=blocking`
- Condition: p99 > **1.3×** 7-day median for **15 minutes**

---

## Validation Checklist (Definition of Done)
1. Dashboard deployed in **staging** with live data for at least **48 hours**.
2. Metrics present and queryable:
   - `inference.request_latency_ms` with tags: model_version, route_name, io_mode, prompt_len_bucket, kv_cache_hit
   - `inference.first_token_latency_ms` for streaming paths
3. Traces:
   - trace attributes include `kernel_variant` and `first_token_ts` (streaming)
   - dashboard trace link opens to a trace showing the required attributes
4. Cardinality and performance:
   - series growth <15% in the primary backend (or approved exception)
   - p50/p95/p99 queries return in **<3 seconds** for a 1-hour window in prod
5. Cohort filters correctly subset series and recompute percentiles.
6. At least one alerting rule is created for streaming p95 regression with paging policy + runbook.
7. QA checklist completed, including:
   - compare streaming vs blocking for the same model/route
   - validate first-token latency distributions match trace timing within ±5%

---

## Rollout Plan
1. Land instrumentation PRs (metrics agent + trace attributes) behind a feature flag.
2. Staging smoke tests + cardinality audit.
3. Enable in prod read-only dashboard for 1 week (no alerts), validate performance.
4. Enable alerts for the high-impact model/route allowlist.
5. Two-week follow-up review:
   - false positive rate
   - sampling costs
   - any required bucket tuning

---

## Appendix: Example metric emission (pseudo-code)
```
// request completion
emit_histogram("inference.request_latency_ms", duration_ms, {
  model_version,
  route_name,
  io_mode, // streaming|blocking
  prompt_len_bucket, // short|medium|long
  kv_cache_hit // true|false|unknown
})

// streaming only: first token
emit_histogram("inference.first_token_latency_ms", first_token_ms, {
  model_version,
  route_name,
  io_mode: "streaming",
  prompt_len_bucket,
  kv_cache_hit
})
```

## Open Questions / Follow-ups
- Add “model compare mode” (two model versions on the same route) as a separate dashboard enhancement.
- Dedicated/private metrics routing for per-customer breakdowns.
- Evaluate pre-computing p95/p99 for the top (model_version, route_name) pairs if query latency regresses.

evidence.title: Compact-collapse heuristics and canvas-clip guardrails for charts, tables, and modal layering
evidence.text:
description:
Problem: High-density dashboard views and canvased charts can overflow, clip awkwardly, or produce inconsistent stacking across Chromium, WebKit, and Firefox when viewport width is reduced and modals open. This causes visual artifacts (half-pixel strokes, shadow cutoffs), keyboard focus traps to break, and interactive table rows to become hard to target on touch devices. Goal: define compact-collapse heuristics for panels, standardized canvas clipping rules for charts and embeddable canvases, and a layering/z-index guardrail for modals/tooltips that behaves consistently across browsers and input modes. Deliver a set of prototypes, handoff-ready specs, and measurable acceptance criteria for engineering to implement in runtime-1.19/console-2026.03.

design_decisions:
Use semantic collapse tiers (primary/secondary) instead of purely pixel-driven shrinking to preserve core info density
Prefer CSS transform + overflow:hidden for canvas containers to avoid layout thrashing and preserve GPU compositing on Safari
Introduce a 10-level z-index scale (base, panel, overlay, modal, modal-top, toast) and require engineering to expose it as CSS tokens
Avoid CSS calc() reliance for critical clipping; instead provide explicit pixel fallbacks for older WebKit engines
Tooltips should render in a dedicated overlay root to avoid stacking context collisions with transformed parent nodes

acceptance_criteria:
Dense dashboard rows collapse to a predictable 2-tier distribution (primary/secondary) under 960px with no content overlap
Canvas-based charts render consistent axis hairlines and shadows across Chrome, Safari, and Firefox at devicePixelRatio 1 and 2
Modal stacking and tooltip z-order follow a deterministic rule set; keyboard focus trap and aria-hidden toggles work when multiple overlays are present
Touch hit targets for table rows and inline controls meet 44px minimum after density adjustments
Prototype validated in Chrome 116+, Safari 16+, Firefox 116+ with documented browser-specific workarounds

deliverables:
Figma prototype (compact + expanded states) with annotated constraints and responsive breakpoints
Interactive CodePen shim demonstrating canvas clip & shadow fixes
Handoff spec PDF with CSS variables, recommended z-index scale, and JS heuristics for collapse thresholds
Acceptance test checklist and cross-browser validation matrix

qa_notes:
Run visual diff on Chrome/Safari/Firefox at DPR 1 and 2 for the dashboard card baseline
Verify focus-trap behavior with nested modals and confirm aria-hidden toggles prevent screen reader access to background content
Check all interactive elements meet 44px touch target after compact collapse rules applied
Record CPU/GPU time for canvas redraw before and after transform-based clipping to ensure no regression

comments:
2026-03-03 - Ava Martinez: Ticket created after exploratory session with PM and frontend eng. Noted recurring clipping bug in Safari when modal opens above a canvas chart.
2026-03-05 - Liam Chen: Drafted breakpoints and compact collapse flow. Built initial Figma frames showing primary/secondary content prioritization.
2026-03-07 - Design review: PM (Ravi Patel) requested explicit touch-target rules and link to analytics showing high error taps in dense lists.
2026-03-09 - Engineering sync: ENG-18910 will prototype canvas clip guard function; agreed to try transform-based clipping and test perf on macOS M1 Safari.
2026-03-11 - QA note: Reproduced half-pixel axis hairline in Firefox when DPR=1.5; added test case to acceptance matrix.
2026-03-12 - Liam Chen: Uploaded interactive CodePen demonstrating different clipping strategies and z-index stacking. Shared for review.
2026-03-13 - Stakeholder review: UX Director approved heuristics; requested final spec include keyboard-only focus flow for nested modals.
