evidence.title: Customer story / case study page template layout + reusable components (Docs site)
evidence.text:
description:
## Context
We’re launching a case study + customer reference program and need a reusable, developer-first customer story page template that can be used across the Docs site (and optionally mirrored on marketing surfaces later). The template must support:
- Quote callouts (short, scannable)
- An architecture diagram block (with caption + light/dark support)
- Metrics/results section with standardized disclaimer language (metrics may be ranges / methodology caveats)

This ticket focuses on page layout and reusable components (blocks) so Marketing/DevEx can publish stories quickly without bespoke design each time.

## Goals
1) Make customer stories easy to skim (developer-first, concrete proof, minimal fluff).
2) Ensure consistent placement and styling for: problem → solution → implementation → results → proof/disclaimers.
3) Provide drop-in components compatible with Docs theming and accessible by default.
4) Create a structure that works for both “public case study” pages and “lightweight story” pages where the customer won’t share exact metrics.

## Non-goals (for this ticket)
- Copywriting for a specific customer story (handled in separate workstreams).
- Implementing the components in code (tracked in ENG tickets/PRs).
- Designing the case studies landing page IA (ENG-9401 + docs PRs).

## Proposed page structure (v1)
1) Hero
- Customer name + optional logo
- One-line outcome statement (e.g., “Dedicated capacity with predictable p95 latency at scale”)
- Deployment mode badges (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- Primary CTA: “Talk to sales” or “Request a demo” (optional for Docs)

2) At-a-glance summary (2-column)
- Use case (e.g., “Ecommerce search + chat assistant”)
- Team / personas (optional)
- Models / workload type (optional, careful with naming if restricted)
- Environment (Dedicated / VPC / on-prem)

3) Challenge / constraints
- Bullet-friendly; include constraints like compliance, latency SLOs, cost targets, regional requirements.

4) Solution (Redwood components used)
- Reference relevant product surfaces (Console, Optimize, routing policies, caching/batching, audit logs/KMS).

5) Implementation
- “What they built” and “How they deployed”
- Include Architecture diagram block

6) Results
- Metric cards (up to 3–5), supporting exact values OR ranges (e.g., “p95 latency: 220–280ms”)
- Include methodology notes as inline footnotes where needed

7) Quote callouts
- Pull quotes placed between sections (ideally after Solution and/or Results)
- Support attribution rules (Name, Title, Company) and “Anonymous customer” pattern

8) Proof / disclaimer block (required)
- Standardized “Metrics and methodology” disclaimer area with consistent styling.
- Must support:
  - “Reported by customer” vs “Measured by Redwood” toggles (copy-only for v1)
  - Ranges instead of exact values
  - Redaction statement (e.g., “Details adjusted to protect confidentiality.”)

9) CTA + related resources
- “See docs” / “Talk to us” / “Read more customer stories”
- Optional: link to eval harness, benchmark post, or product docs

## Components to design (reusable blocks)
- CustomerStoryHero
- BadgeRow (deployment mode, industry tags)
- SummaryGrid
- QuoteCallout (short + long variants)
- MetricCard (exact value) + MetricCardRange (range) + MetricFootnote style
- ArchitectureDiagramBlock (image, caption, alt text guidance, ‘Open image’ affordance)
- DisclaimerBlock (standardized, with info icon)
- CTASection (secondary, consistent across stories)

## Content + legal constraints
- Support “logo hidden” and “attribution hidden” variants.
- Metrics may be:
  - exact values,
  - ranges,
  - directional improvements only (e.g., “reduced p95 latency” without numbers).
- Must include a dedicated area where Legal-approved disclaimers can be placed without reworking layout.

## Accessibility requirements
- Quote callouts must maintain contrast and not rely on color alone.
- Metric cards must be readable with large text scaling.
- Architecture diagram must have:
  - required alt text field guidance,
  - optional long description pattern (link or expandable text) for complex diagrams.

## Deliverables
- Figma frame(s) for:
  - Full page template (desktop + mobile)
  - Component specs / variants (logo on/off, attribution on/off, metrics exact/range)
  - Example content filled in (use Northwind outline placeholders; no customer-confidential copy)
- Hand-off notes for DevEx/Engineering (spacing, typography tokens, responsive behavior)

## Acceptance criteria
- Page template works with:
  - at least 1 quote callout,
  - 1 architecture diagram,
  - 3 metric cards + disclaimer block.
- Has documented variants for anonymized stories (no logo, anonymous quote attribution).
- Clear guidance for where the metrics disclaimer goes and how it behaves on mobile.
- Components are consistent with Docs typography and spacing; no one-off colors.
- Accessibility checklist passed (contrast, semantic hierarchy guidance, alt text pattern).

## Links / references
- Docs implementation context: sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-4821-add-case-studies-landing-page-and-template.json
- Navigation ticket: ENG-9401
- Program owner: Camila Reyes
- Messaging/narrative: Soojin Lee
- Technical validation/diagrams: Markus Klein / Simran Kaur

## Notes
If we can’t support fully interactive disclosure patterns in v1, we should still design the disclaimer block to be future-proof (space + structure) and keep v1 copy-only.

comments:
2025-10-03 (Soojin Lee): Strong preference for developer-first scanning: avoid large hero blocks; keep headline + proof above the fold. Also please include a pattern for when we’re only allowed to publish metric ranges or directional improvements.
2025-10-06 (Markus Klein): For the architecture diagram block, we should assume diagrams come from Solutions Eng exports (SVG/PNG). We need a consistent max width and a way to open in a new tab for readability. Also please include a short caption field (1–2 lines) for quick context.
2025-10-08 (Michael Grant): Disclaimers need to be visually separated from marketing copy. Recommend an always-present “Metrics and methodology” section to reduce the risk of a story being published without the required caveats. Also need an anonymization sentence pattern when customer requests it.
2025-10-10 (Tyler Benson): Operationally, Marketing will reuse these blocks across multiple pages. Any component variants should map to simple markdown/MDX frontmatter toggles (logo_on/off, attribution_on/off, metrics_mode=exact|range|directional). Even if engineering does the mapping later, naming the variants now will help.
2025-10-14 (Camila Reyes): Please include an example of a ‘reference-call ready’ quote callout: something that highlights reliability/fallbacks and doesn’t mention confidential infrastructure details. We’ve had customers want quote edits even after approval—keeping callouts short helps.
2025-10-18 (Update): Design delivered in Figma with desktop/mobile layouts + component variants. Added explicit anonymized attribution pattern and standardized disclaimer block placement directly under Results.
2025-10-21 (Closeout): Hand-off notes shared with DevEx and linked in docs PR review. Engineering confirmed the layout can be implemented with existing Docs tokens + a small set of new components.

evidence.title: Publish Northwind Commerce customer story + standard metrics disclaimer
evidence.text:
release_notes:
Docs: Added first public case study (Northwind Commerce) to /case-studies, including an approved quote block, architecture diagram, and a standardized metrics disclaimer component used across stories.

description:
Summary: Publishes the first customer story on the docs site (Northwind Commerce) and introduces a standardized metrics disclaimer block that we can reuse across future case studies. This PR is intended to be the canonical example/template for subsequent stories (Helios/Atlas/etc.) and aligns language with the approved messaging pillars for performance economics + reliability/fallback + Dedicated capacity. What’s included: (1) New case study page for Northwind Commerce with approved positioning, quotes, and a metrics section that supports exact values or ranges. (2) Standardized metrics disclaimer component + content guidelines (public-facing) so we don’t repeat bespoke legal language on every story. (3) Architecture diagram asset wiring (static file reference + alt text + caption) and a small update to the Case Studies landing page to surface Northwind as the first published entry. Notes/constraints: Metrics are published as ranges per customer preference; the page avoids hardware-specific claims beyond what was validated by SE, and links to internal proof sources are kept out of the public page. Support note: SUP-3812 (transient p95 spike) is resolved; the published metrics reflect the stable window (see internal notes in the PR discussion).

review_conversation:
Soojin Lee (Product Marketing) — 2025-10-25: Messaging looks aligned overall. Two nits: (1) Avoid implying automatic multi-region failover unless we explicitly say it’s policy-driven routing. (2) In the headline metrics callout, can we phrase cost as “lowered $/1M tokens” rather than “cut costs by X%” since this is range-based? Also please ensure the CTA points to Dedicated/Private evaluation rather than generic sign-up.
Ethan Wallace — 2025-10-25: Updated reliability language to “policy-driven routing + fallback to compatible variants” and rewrote the cost callout to “lowered $/1M tokens (range)” with the disclaimer immediately below. CTA now points to “Talk to us about Dedicated” (sales form) and keeps the hosted API link secondary.
Markus Klein (Solutions Eng) — 2025-10-26: Diagram is close. Please change “GPU pool autoscaling” label to “Dedicated capacity + burst policy” and add a note that prefix caching is workload-dependent. Also the section “Implementation” mentions “kernel selection” — that’s true but reads too internal; can we keep it at “optimized runtime paths”?
Ethan Wallace — 2025-10-26: Done. Diagram labels updated + caption includes “prefix caching enabled where applicable”. Reworded kernel language to “optimized runtime paths selected for the model + sequence profile.”
Simran Kaur (SE) — 2025-10-27: Metrics table: can we add measurement method for p95 latency (window + region + payload type) so it’s defensible? Doesn’t need to be super detailed, just “measured at the Redwood gateway across production traffic” etc. Also, please add alt text for the diagram for accessibility.
Ethan Wallace — 2025-10-27: Added a “How it was measured” line under the metrics section (p95 at gateway; 7-day trailing window; typical request shape described at high level). Added descriptive alt text and kept the diagram caption concise.
Michael Grant (Legal) — 2025-10-28: Disclaimer language needs two tweaks: (1) Make clear that “results vary” and metrics are customer-reported/validated but not a guarantee. (2) Add revocation note is not necessary on page (it’s in the consent), but do add “published with permission” and avoid “certified” wording anywhere. Also please remove the word “guaranteed” in the uptime paragraph (even if it’s describing an internal SLO).
Ethan Wallace — 2025-10-28: Updated disclaimer component: “Metrics are from Northwind’s production deployment and/or Redwood observability where available; results will vary by workload and configuration; nothing herein is a guarantee.” Added “Published with permission.” Removed “guaranteed” and replaced with “targeted” / “SLA-backed (contract-specific)” phrasing.
Tyler Benson (Marketing Ops) — 2025-10-29: Please ensure the story is registered in the case study registry with the correct slug and that the landing page card uses the approved short blurb. Also, can we add UTM-safe outbound links (no hardcoded UTM, just link to canonical pages)?
Ethan Wallace — 2025-10-29: Registry entry added; landing card uses the approved blurb. Removed hardcoded UTMs and pointed to canonical /contact-sales and /dedicated pages.
Markus Klein — 2025-10-30: Final pass looks good. One last thing: please add a small note under the routing diagram that fallback is configurable and may be disabled for strict pinning.
Ethan Wallace — 2025-10-30: Added a one-sentence note under the diagram caption: “Fallback policies are configurable and can be disabled when strict model pinning is required.”
Soojin Lee — 2025-10-30: Approved.
Michael Grant — 2025-10-30: Approved (language matches the consent boundaries).
Markus Klein — 2025-10-30: Approved.

question: What was the root cause and planned server-side fix for the March 2026 incident where function-call webhook callbacks were retried after a timeout and the JSON payload stayed the same, but the HMAC signature header changed between the first delivery and the retry due to gzip/encoding differences?

evidence.title: Webhook signature mismatch after client-side retry causes duplicated function-call side effects
evidence.text:
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart reports duplicated downstream side effects from function-calls triggered via Redwood streaming API. The customer observed that when their edge worker (Cloudflare) hits a transient timeout while processing our function-call callback, Redwood retries delivery. However, the first callback was received by BrightCart but the webhook verification signature they compute (HMAC-SHA256 of the canonicalized body) does not match the signature header in our retry request. As a result their endpoint returns 4xx for the retry while accepting the original, and they see duplicate processing of the same business action (order confirmation webhooks).

Impact:
- Duplicate order confirmations observed for ~0.3% of calls from the BrightCart integration over the last 24h (~120 duplicates).
- Customer is enterprise and reports these duplicates trigger payment reconciliation issues and manual support overhead.

Observed behavior:
- Initial callback arrives and is accepted (200). Shortly after, a retry from Redwood is sent (due to an intermediate timeout at customer's edge). The retry contains the same payload but the signature header (x-rw-signature) differs. BrightCart's verification rejects this retry (401) and their application performs a compensating re-processing that results in duplicate side effects.

Expected behavior:
- Retries should be byte-for-byte identical or signatures should verify equivalently after any transport changes. If any canonicalization occurs (gzip, newline normalization), we should surface that or avoid signing the body in a way that changes between attempts.

Key customer details and integration notes:
- BrightCart deployed a Cloudflare Worker that forwards the webhook to their internal API. The worker does minimal processing but performs an auto-decompression step in some fast-paths.
- They use our JS SDK (streaming + funcall callbacks).
- Their verification computes HMAC on the canonical JSON: compacted keys, 
  but it expects incoming body to match exactly what was signed earlier by Redwood's callback flow.

Attachments (provided by customer):
- Example successful callback (raw body and x-rw-signature header).
- Example retry that failed verification (raw body and x-rw-signature header).
- Cloudflare edge logs showing the timing and a transient 504 between their worker and origin roughly coincident with the retry window.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Create a streaming session that triggers a function-call to BrightCart's webhook endpoint.
2) At the edge (simulate Cloudflare), force origin-to-worker request to experience a small timeout (drop the ACK) so Redwood considers delivery not confirmed and triggers retry path.
3) Inspect first and subsequent delivery bodies and x-rw-signature headers.


steps_to_reproduce:
Repro notes provided by Support: We have a small harness that uses the JS SDK to stream a funcall. On the receiving side, run a local server that records request body bytes and signature header. Simulate an edge by inserting a transparent proxy that can drop the origin upstream response after the first delivery so Redwood triggers the retry. Compare raw bytes of first delivery vs retry. (Customer provided sample harness.)

logs:
Customer-provided excerpt: 
--- first callback (accepted) ---
POST /callback 200
x-rw-signature: sha256=3f9b...
body: {"order_id":"ORD-1001","status":"confirmed"}

--- retry callback (rejected) ---
POST /callback 401
x-rw-signature: sha256=7a1c...
body: {"order_id":"ORD-1001","status":"confirmed"}

Cloudflare worker logs: origin returned 504 after 1.2s, worker forwarded first request to origin then responded to client before origin ack completed. Timing suggests client-side decompression path changed body bytes before signing on the retry path.

investigation_notes:
Initial triage by Support (2026-03-11):
- Confirmed duplicate side effects and presence of differing signatures.
- Reproduced locally using customer's harness; observed that when the edge proxy auto-decompresses gzip payloads on retry path (to compute body for forwarding) the whitespace and unicode escaping differed in the raw bytes even though JSON values were identical.
- Hypothesis: our signing step currently signs the post-transport body representation (content bytes) and a downstream intermediate (edge worker / proxy) decompression/re-serialization can mutate the bytes between attempts. If retries use a different transport encoding (e.g., first attempt gzipped, retry sent uncompressed or with slightly different header order), signatures will diverge.
- Checked delivery service: initial attempt uses chunked gzip path; retry falls back to non-chunked encoding to satisfy a different upstream route. This behavior was triggered by a gateway route selection policy that aims for smaller retries.

Observations from code and infra (SRE):
- api-gateway signs the payload after compression step. The signing call is currently invoked after the compression encoder. The retry code path triggers a different encoder instance which produced identical logical JSON but not identical bytes (spacing and JSON key order stable but gzip container differences and CRLF normalization changed raw bytes).
- Edge proxies (Cloudflare) have auto-decompress/inflate behavior for certain responses which can lead to the worker forwarding a slightly re-serialized body back to origin, affecting the bytes that BrightCart sees in the retry chain.

Temporary mitigation recommended to customer (2026-03-12):
- BrightCart adjusted their verification to compute HMAC on a canonical canonicalized JSON (compact serialization, sorted keys, normalized UTF-8) rather than raw bytes; this reduces rejections but is not ideal for long-term cryptographic guarantees.

comments:
2026-03-11 10:22 - Support (Marco Ruiz): Thanks for the report Aisha — we've started triage and will attempt a reproduction with the harness. Can you confirm whether you saw any retry headers (x-rw-retry-count) on the failed delivery?
2026-03-11 11:05 - Customer (BrightCart - DevOps, Linh Tran): We do see x-rw-retry-count: 1 on the retry. Attached the raw payloads and worker logs to the ticket (uploaded).
2026-03-11 14:40 - Support (Marco Ruiz): Repro completed locally. Observed differing signatures; initial attempt bytes were gzipped with specific timestamp in gzip header; retry path produced a gzipped payload with different gzip envelope metadata causing signature mismatch. We're engaging SRE to review signing placement.
2026-03-12 09:15 - SRE (Nikhil Desai): Found signing is performed post-compression. Opening a change to sign the canonical logical payload (pre-compression) to ensure retries that re-encode still verify. Raised internal PR for discussion: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2197
2026-03-12 16:00 - Customer (Linh Tran): As a temporary workaround we canonicalize input on our side; that dropped duplicates to near 0, but we'd prefer the provider guarantee. Please keep us posted on rollout timeline.
2026-03-13 08:30 - Support (Marco Ruiz): Noted. SRE estimates configuration change + canary in staging will be ready in 48 hours. We'll schedule a staged rollout and keep this ticket updated.

resolution:
Workaround: Customer implemented canonical JSON HMAC verification which mitigated duplicates. Planned fix: move signing to pre-compression canonical payload representation so that retries that differ only by transport encoding still verify. Change set created and internal PR open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2197. Rollout plan: canary in staging -> canary in two prod clusters -> full rollout. Post-deploy verification script will run against BrightCart's harness. No permanent rollback planned. Follow-ups: update webhook integration docs to recommend canonicalization best-practices and add a header x-rw-canonicalization-version to indicate what representation was signed.

follow_up_actions:
- SRE to land PR and coordinate canary (owner: Nikhil Desai).
- Support to coordinate BrightCart for canary tests (owner: Marco Ruiz).
- Docs owner to add canonicalization guidance and consumer verification examples (owner: DevEx team).
- Monitor duplicates for 72h post-rollout and report to customer.

notes:
This ticket is distinct from other funcall idempotency duplicates as root cause is signing after transport encoding, not missing idempotency tokens. Consider auditing other signing flows that sign post-transport bytes.

evidence.title: Signed webhook callback mismatches after OAuth refresh during long-lived streaming retry -> duplicate tool invocations
evidence.text:
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicate downstream tool executions when a long-lived streaming request is retried after an OAuth token refresh. The customer uses our streaming SDK (Python) with an external webhook sink that verifies HMAC signatures (header: X-RW-SIG).

Impact:
- Duplicate external operations (billing webhooks, downstream provisioning) observed intermittently for ~3 customers on Dedicated tier.
- Reproducible under load with stream migration / region failover.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant (TellusFin) running prod in us-east with secondary eu-west failover.
- SDKs: python 1.12.3, go 1.12.0 (edge), ts 1.11.7.

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Open streaming function call with functions/toolchain enabled and a callback URL that validates HMAC signature (X-RW-SIG).
2) Simulate long-running generation (20-40s) and induce an OAuth refresh on client side by forcing token expiry mid-stream.
3) Cause a short network interruption (5s) or trigger region failover.
4) SDK reconnects, performs retry; callback is replayed but the downstream service sometimes treats it as a new invocation and performs the action again.

Observed behavior:
- Downstream verifies signature but intermittently rejects because signature encoding differs (base64 vs base64url and padding differences). When rejection occurs client retries, but idempotency-key header is sometimes rotated/truncated during the SDK's token refresh code path, so server receives what looks like a fresh invocation.
- Platform logs show the original tool invocation completed but the retry was accepted and executed again, producing duplicate side effects.

Expected behavior:
- Retries should be deduplicated by idempotency key regardless of token refresh. Signature encoding normalization should not cause valid retries to be treated as new requests.

Attachments / sample logs provided by customer (redacted):
- request headers (orig): X-RW-SIG: HMAC-SHA256 base64=QmFzZTY0UGFkZGVk...
- request headers (retry after refresh): X-RW-SIG: HMAC-SHA256 base64url=QmFzZTY0UGFkZGVk (no padding)
- idempotency-key sometimes shows suffix ":refresh" on retry in python-sdk logs.
- Correlated platform trace: trace_id=tr_0a3f... shows two completions for tool-run id tr_0a3f-run-12


comments:
2026-03-10 11:02 - Aisha Patel: Initial report from TellusFin: duplicate webhook side effects after long streaming session and token refresh. Attached minimal reproduction script.
2026-03-10 12:10 - Support (Miguel Torres): Acknowledged. Requested request/response headers, idempotency-key values, and platform trace IDs. Escalating to SRE for routing/serving-runtime correlation.
2026-03-11 09:45 - SRE (Lin Zhao): Found traces showing two 'tool_completed' events 18s apart but same client request_id. Noting signature verification failures around retry window. Adding auth team.
2026-03-12 15:22 - Auth (Priya Menon): Reproduced locally. Our verification library treats base64url and base64 as distinct encodings. Some SDKs produce base64url without padding for new signatures after JWT refresh.

investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: During the SDK OAuth refresh path, the code that re-signs outgoing webhook callbacks uses a different base64 encoder (base64url) and does not preserve original padding. Additionally, the python SDK's retry wrapper appends a small suffix to the idempotency-key when it detects a refresh event ("...:refresh"), which prevents server-side dedupe because dedupe key mismatches.

Evidence collected:
- SDK client logs show idempotency-key 'tf-req-5001' then 'tf-req-5001:refresh' after refresh.
- Platform webhook verifier rejects base64url-signed payloads when configured to expect standard base64; rejection triggers client to assume callback failed and retry.
- Recreated in a controlled test with SDK v1.12.3 where forcing token refresh produced base64url signatures.

Priority next steps being executed:
- Auth team to relax signature verifier to accept base64url and canonicalize both encodings to a canonical bytes representation. (In progress)

resolution:
Mitigations applied (2026-03-13):
1) Server-side: webhook verifier updated to accept both standard base64 and base64url, and to normalize padding before verification (hotfix deployed to edge-proxies in us-east/eu-west).
2) SDK-side: temporary guidance issued: do not mutate idempotency-key during refresh. Customer instructed to pin idempotency_key in application layer for critical toolchains. Patch scheduled for SDKs to remove ':refresh' suffix and to preserve original idempotency header across retries (PR referenced).

Effect: After hotfix, TellusFin reported no further duplicates in 48h window under the same test.


follow_up_actions:
1) Ship SDK patch to ensure idempotency-key is invariant across OAuth refresh and retries (PR https://github.com/redwood/inference-sdk/pull/4189). Target release: python 1.12.4, go 1.12.1, ts 1.11.8.
2) Add canonicalization tests to CI that exercise base64 vs base64url signature formats and ensure verifier accepts both.
3) Update Confluence runbook: 'Webhook signature mismatches & OAuth refresh' with triage steps and customer-facing mitigation guidance.
4) Outreach: Customer success to notify TellusFin when SDK patch is published and offer a short audit of their webhook verification logic.
5) Postmortem if further duplicates are observed; consider adding server-side idempotency mapping that tolerates small suffixes for 5 minutes for high-risk customers.

evidence.title: Binary payload integrity errors after SDK retry with gzipped function outputs
evidence.text:
description:
Issue summary:
Customer receives integrity / checksum failures for binary artifacts returned from function-calling outputs when the request is retried by the Python SDK. Failures only appear in production on the customer's Private deployment after an API retry path (client-side backoff) and when the runtime returns a gzipped binary blob as part of a funcall response payload.

Impact:
- Arbor Analytics ETL pipelines intermittently report corrupted attachment contents and raise exceptions.
- A subset of requests (~0.3% of funcall responses) get invalid checksums leading to failed downstream processing and manual re-ingest.
- Customer is on Enterprise plan and on a Private deployment with HSM-backed key rotation enabled.

Environment:
- Redwood Private deployment (customer-managed control plane)
- Region: us-east-1
- Python SDK v1.8.3 (pinned)
- API gateway: HTTP/2 fronting internal gRPC to serving runtime
- Serving runtime: redwood-llm-v2-large with gzip content compression enabled for funcall outputs
- HSM: periodic API key rotation during nightly window (03:30-04:00 UTC)

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1. Submit a funcall request that returns a binary attachment (e.g., generated report.tar.gz encoded in base64 inside funcall result).
2. Simulate transient network error on the client so the SDK applies its retry/backoff (observed during short 502/timeout).
3. On retry, the response sometimes decodes to binary with invalid checksum when written to disk by the customer's consumer.

Observed behavior:
- The Python SDK logs show a retry and a subsequent 200 response.
- The funcall.response.body appears to contain base64 that decodes but the binary is corrupted (tar fails to extract).
- SRE traces show the first attempt returned compressed payload with Transfer-Encoding: chunked over HTTP/2; second attempt response path shows identical content-length but different content encoding header.

Expected behavior:
- Retries should result in identical, bit-exact payloads for the same logical response or the retry should be detected and ignored if dedup semantics are used. No corruption should occur as a result of retries.

Logs and artifacts provided by customer (sanitized):
- SDK debug trace (attached) showing request id and retry sequence: req=arbor-req-9982 attempt=1 -> timeout, attempt=2 -> 200
- Base64 strings from both attempts (hex diff attached in support bundle)
- Serving runtime request trace: trace-id 2c3f6a showing gzipped payload returned on attempt 1 and attempt 2 with differing content-encoding headers in the edge layer.

Hypothesis (initial):
- Edge/ingress layer is performing header normalization on retry paths (HTTP/2 connection reuse + proxy rewriting) and occasionally drops or reorders content-encoding headers for chunked gzip responses.
- The SDK's retry path assumes idempotent raw body bytes and directly decodes base64 without validating content-encoding consistency across attempts.
- HSM key rotation timing may cause subtle changes in how binary is streamed (observed correlation with nightly rotation window), but not the primary cause.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Customer disabled gzip compression for funcall outputs in their Private runtime config; this mitigated the corruption rate in their environment to near zero.
- Recommended short-term: upgrade to Python SDK preview v1.9.0 (contains additional validation) and enable SDK-level content-encoding sanity checks as a stopgap.

Next steps (investigation):
- SRE to check ingress proxy (internal Edge) logs for header mutation on connection reuse and retries.
- SDK team to add decoding-time content-encoding validation and optional conservative retry semantics for funcall binary payloads.
- Runtime team to evaluate whether we can ensure stable content-encoding across retries (avoid rewriting headers on retried requests).

References:
- Customer-provided support bundle: arbor-560412-bundle.tar.gz (stored in support ticket attachments)
- Related internal note: INT-2215 (ingress header-rewrite experiments)


comments:
2026-03-10 09:14 - Asha Patel (Support): Acknowledged receipt of the report from Arbor Analytics. Requested SDK debug logs and serving traces. SLA due 2026-03-11.
2026-03-10 10:03 - Arbor Support Engineer (Customer): Uploaded SDK trace and two base64 payload samples (attempt1, attempt2). Noted failures cluster around 03:40 UTC in their environment.
2026-03-10 15:22 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Start investigating ingress proxy. Found intermittent header rewrite on reused HTTP/2 streams when content was chunked and gzip: occasionally Content-Encoding header was omitted on replayed responses.
2026-03-11 08:45 - Priya Nair (SDK): Reproduced locally by constructing a proxy that drops content-encoding on second response. Confirmed Python SDK v1.8.3 does not compare content-encoding between attempts prior to base64 decode. Preparing patch to add a warning and optional strict mode.
2026-03-12 11:05 - Miguel Santos (SRE): Deployed a canary fix to ingress proxy to preserve content-encoding for replayed responses in private deployments. Monitoring for reduction in incidents.
2026-03-13 09:30 - Arbor Analytics (Customer): Confirmed that after disabling gzip at runtime the corruption incidents dropped to zero across a 48h window. Will wait for SDK patch and ingress fix before re-enabling compression.
2026-03-13 12:10 - Asha Patel (Support): Recommended next release steps: (1) SDK strict decoding release note; (2) ingress stable rollout; (3) follow-up runbook for customers to disable compression if immediate impact observed. Assigned owners in INT-2215 and PR #1342.
2026-03-13 15:00 - Priya Nair (SDK): Opened draft PR adding content-encoding validation and an opt-in strict_retry_mode flag. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/457

investigation_notes:
Edge layer reproduced header drop when multiplexed streams used and chunked transfer encoding combined with gzip; implemented guard to copy content-encoding header from original upstream response to replayed response.
SDK change will: add content-encoding check between attempts, fall back to not decoding if enc mismatch, log error, and surface non-idempotent warning to customer.
Customer private deploy had HSM rotation during incident window but root cause appears independent; still coordinating with infra to ensure key rotation does not affect streaming semantics.

evidence.title: Asynchronous webhook ACK race causes duplicated chained function/tool executions on retry
evidence.text:
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (DocuLend, dedicated) reports duplicate downstream side-effects when using chained function/tool-calls with asynchronous webhook callbacks. The customer uses the Python SDK to request a function call that triggers their webhook; the webhook returns a 202 Accepted (async processing). When the client or SDK retried due to a streaming disconnect, the same function call was executed twice by the customer backend.

Impact:
- Duplicate downstream jobs (billing and document-signing) processed twice for several high-value requests; customer reported financial and user-experience impact.
- Occurred intermittently under moderate load during a spike; reproducible on demand in our environment.

Environment:
- Redwood Hosted API, prod us-east region, customer on Dedicated pool.
- SDKs used: python-redwood 2.3.1 and js-redwood 1.8.0 in different integrations.
- Models: redwood/gptx-3b 

Steps to reproduce (minimal):
1) Customer config: chained function flow where model triggers a function call: {"name": "start_job", "arguments": {...}}.
2) Their webhook handler immediately responds 202 Accepted and processes the job asynchronously (job created, queued, processed later).
3) Client opens a streaming generation connection (Python streaming chunking) and receives a partial response. Mid-stream the connection is closed (network blip).
4) Client SDK retries the request using automatic retry policy (idempotency not explicitly provided by customer).
5) The model (or the server-side function router) issues the function call again; webhook receives a second invocation and creates a second job.

Expected behavior:
- Retries should not cause duplicate downstream side effects when the webhook accepted the callback and returned 202. Either: (a) SDK should surface a clear way to attach a per-action idempotency token to the function call; or (b) the serving/runtime should not re-emit an already-acknowledged function call when an acknowledgement was already proxied upstream.

Actual behavior:
- The function call is sent twice during a retry scenario; DocuLend sees two queued jobs.

Logs / example traces (customer-provided):
- Customer webhook trace: 
  POST /callbacks/start_job 202 
  X-Req-Id: dl-req-1142
  payload.job_id: job-20260308-88

  POST /callbacks/start_job 202 
  X-Req-Id: dl-req-1143
  payload.job_id: job-20260308-89

- From SDK side: python client shows reconnect and retry logs: 
  INFO: redwood.sdk.stream: connection closed by server, attempting retry (attempt 1)
  INFO: redwood.sdk.request: retrying request without idempotency key

Attachments: sample recording and http traces provided by customer (S3 link), anonymized request/response dump included.

steps_to_reproduce:
Configure chained function call that posts to an async webhook returning 202
Open a streaming completion request from Python SDK and induce a mid-stream disconnect
Allow SDK to retry automatically (no manual idempotency header set)
Observe duplicate POSTs to customer's webhook and two downstream job entries

observed_logs:
POST /callbacks/start_job 202 X-Req-Id: dl-req-1142 payload.job_id: job-20260308-88
POST /callbacks/start_job 202 X-Req-Id: dl-req-1143 payload.job_id: job-20260308-89
INFO: redwood.sdk.stream: connection closed by server, attempting retry (attempt 1)
INFO: redwood.sdk.request: retrying request without idempotency key

comments:
Customer Support (Aisha): Thank you for the details — we can reproduce this in our staging cluster; assigning to Eng/SRE for deeper investigation.
SRE (Ben): Initial hypothesis: SDK retry logic replays the function call because we only consider final success when function execution completes. If callback returns 202 (accepted), we treat that as success upstream but the streaming retry path may re-emit before the ACK is fully recorded in our request-state store.
Customer (DocuLend Engineer): We rely on 202 because jobs are enqueued for long-running processing. Our webhook cannot synchronously confirm completion. How should we deduplicate from our side?
Support (Aisha): Short-term workaround: include a client-generated idempotency token in function_call arguments yourself (e.g., job_client_id) and dedupe on webhook side. We'll follow up with engineering on server-side guards.
Eng (Ben): Creating follow-ups to evaluate persisting function-call ACKs earlier in the pipeline and to add a recommended SDK helper for attaching a per-function idempotency header. See linked PR that prototypes an option: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821

investigation_notes:
Reproduced in prod-like dedicated pool with synthetic load (test customer account).
Tracing shows two distinct server-side function-call events emitted with two different internal event ids; both were delivered to webhook because webhook ACK was 202 and we did not mark the call as 'durably recorded' until later in the pipeline.
Root cause hypothesis: race between streaming connection retry path and durable write of function-call metadata to the event-store. When reconnect/retry occurs before durable write completes, the request is replayed and results in a duplicate downstream invocation.
Confirmed that using an explicit idempotency key in the function_call arguments prevents duplicate jobs in our reproduction environment (customer-side dedupe).

resolution:
Workarounds and fixes:
1) Customer workaround (immediate): Add a stable client-generated idempotency token in the function call payload (e.g., job_client_id) and perform deduping in your webhook using that token. Ensure your webhook returns 200 for an already-seen token and 202 for a newly enqueued job to avoid semantic confusion.
2) SDK guidance (short-term): Document recommended pattern for per-action idempotency (examples for Python/TS/Go) in docs.
3) Platform fix (mid-term): Engineering to change function-call pipeline to mark an invocation as 'acknowledged' earlier (persist pre-delivery id) or to respect a function-call idempotency header when present. A patch PR is in review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821.
4) Long-term: Add SDK-level option to attach auto-generated per-action idempotency keys and propagate them to webhooks and audit logs so downstreams can dedupe reliably.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-OPS task created to harden durable-write ordering and add a test covering async webhook 202 scenarios.
- Notify customer onboarding/solutions team once SDK helper is released so they can update DocuLend integration.

notes_for_cs:
Recommend customer implement client-side job_client_id idempotency token in short term. CS to follow up after platform patch is released. Provide sample code snippets for Python/TS/Go demonstrating pattern.

evidence.title: Batched attachments with gzip-encoded payloads cause duplicate tool executions on retry via Python async iterator
evidence.text:
description:
Issue summary:
Customer uses the Python async iterator SDK to send batched requests that include multiple attachments (binary blobs) per request. They gzip each batch on the client side. When the server returns a transient 202+retryable ack (internal queue enqueue), the SDK retries and we observe duplicate tool/function executions downstream (duplicate webhook calls and duplicate DB side effects).

Impact:
- Multiple duplicate downstream webhook posts and side effects for a small subset (~0.6%) of batched requests during transient enqueue failures.
- Customer reports data duplication and billing noise for high-volume ingestion job.
- Affects dedicated customers using client-side gzip + async iterator batching pattern.

Environment:
- Customer: SwellHealth (dedicated cluster)
- SDK: sdk-python v1.14.2 (async iterator example)
- Runtime: dedicated serving pool in prod-us-east
- Proxy: edge-sidecar with gzip passthrough enabled
- Observed on models: redwood-gpt-3.5-large (primary), also reproduced on llama-2-13b in test runs

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1. Use async for chunk in client.stream_batches(...): send batch that contains 3 attachments (binary ECG, JSON metadata, PDF) compressed with gzip at client before sending.
2. Server returns 202 Accepted with body {"enqueue": "ok", "trace": "..."} but internal queue intermittently times out when attempting to ack.
3. SDK interprets 202 as transient and retries the entire batch (full gzip binary) after applying backoff.
4. Downstream worker consumes both messages from queue (original and retried) and triggers the same tool/function twice (webhook POST + DB write).

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate webhook POSTs with identical payloads and same content checksum but different request IDs.
- No idempotency key present in the batched/gzipped envelope because the client included per-item IDs inside the compressed payload, not in the request headers or envelope-level idempotency metadata.

Expected behavior:
- Retries should either be deduplicated server-side by an envelope-level idempotency key or the SDK should ensure a stable idempotency token is attached to the request header even when payloads are gzipped by client.

Logs and traces (redacted):
- API gateway logs show repeated POSTs for the same client session id within a 2s window: request_id=req-17a3, req-17a4
- Serving runtime trace: enqueue attempt 1 -> internal queue timeout (timeout after 550ms) -> SDK retry -> enqueue attempt 2 -> queue ok -> downstream worker processed message id ws-993 -> processed again id ws-994
- Edge proxy logs show content-encoding: gzip on both requests; content-length identical.

Customer-provided code snippet (sanitized):
async for batch in batch_generator():
    compressed = gzip.compress(serialize(batch))
    await client.stream_send(compressed, headers={"Content-Encoding": "gzip"})

Workaround attempted by customer:
- Client-side dedupe table (in-memory) keyed by per-item UUIDs inside payload. Reduced duplicates but did not eliminate them because some retry windows cross process restarts.

Notes:
- This pattern differs from single-request idempotency since the idempotency data is buried inside a compressed envelope and not visible to middle proxies or the enqueueer.
- There are existing tickets about idempotency header truncation and token rotation, but this is specifically about envelope-level idempotency and client-side gzip in the async iterator pattern.


comments:
2026-03-10 09:12 - Support (Maya Patel): Triage completed. Assigned to SRE for replication in dedicated infra. Asked customer for sample batch ID and timestamps.
2026-03-10 11:05 - Customer (SwellHealth - devops@swllhealth.com): Provided sample request_ids req-17a3 and req-17a4, and worker ids ws-993/ws-994. Confirmed sdk-python v1.14.2 and they are compressing client-side.
2026-03-11 08:43 - SRE (Ethan Clark): Reproduced locally using async iterator + gzip envelope. Observed server returns 202 on simulated transient queue ack and SDK issues full retry. Added debug logs to show envelope lacks envelope-id header. Referenced linked issue SUP-314159 for batching dedupe history.
2026-03-11 14:22 - SDK Eng (Leah Huang): Noted SDK behavior is to retry on 202 when ack flow indicates transient error. SDK currently does not synthesize an envelope-level idempotency header when payload is compressed. Investigating safe header injection semantics for compressed envelopes.
2026-03-12 09:10 - SRE (Ethan Clark): Ran a small canary with server-side dedupe when content-length and checksum match within 5s window. Canary prevented duplicates in test harness for this pattern. However this approach might be risky for other workloads (false dedupe).
2026-03-12 13:30 - Support (Maya Patel): Notified customer of temporary mitigation and next steps: a) short-term server-side dedupe canary b) SDK patch to add X-Envelope-Id header when async iterator is used and client sets Content-Encoding:gzip. Waiting on SDK PR.
2026-03-12 16:05 - SDK Eng (Leah Huang): Opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/4521 to add deterministic envelope id generation (uuid4 v5-like with client session + sequence) and surface header X-Envelope-Id unless customer opts out. Marked for review.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: duplicate executions caused by lack of envelope-level idempotency when client compresses payload. Confirmed by reproducer. Alternate hypothesis (header truncation at proxy) was ruled out because edge proxy preserved Content-Encoding and headers; both requests had identical lengths and gzip metadata. Packet-level traces show identical binary bodies. Evidence points to SDK retry semantics combined with missing envelope idempotency. Server-side short-lived dedupe works in canary but could create false positives in high-throughput heterogeneous workloads. Proposed long-term fix: SDK-generated X-Envelope-Id for batched async streams plus guidance to include explicit envelope-id when using client-side compression. Also document pattern in support KB.

resolution_notes:
In Progress - short-term server-side dedupe canary enabled for the customer's dedicated pool (monitored). SDK patch PR #4521 created and under review to add a deterministic envelope id header for async iterator batched sends when Content-Encoding:gzip is present. Post-merge action items: release patch in v1.14.3, notify affected customers, add KB article outlining recommended pattern (envelope id header + per-item ids). Follow-up: measure false-dedupe rate in 30-day canary and consider adding idempotency verification in serving runtime to safely dedupe based on envelope-id + model+route.

follow_up_actions:
Merge SDK PR and ship v1.14.3 patch
Create KB: 'Avoiding duplicates with client-side gzip in async batching'
Monitor canary false-dedupe rate for 30 days
Consider API contract update to recommend envelope-id header for compressed envelopes
